title.zh: 卷一百〇一 列傳第五十一: 李乂 薛登 韋湊 韓思復 張廷珪 王求禮 辛替否
title.en: Volume 101 Biographies 51: Li Yi, Xue Deng, Wei Cou, Han Sifu, Zhang Tinggui, Wang Qiuli, Xin Tifou
title.raw: 卷一百〇一 列傳第五十一: 李乂 薛登 韋湊 韓思復 張廷珪 王求禮 辛替否 Volume 101 Biographies 51: Li Yi, Xue Deng, Wei Cou, Han Sifu, Zhang Tinggui, Wang Qiuli, Xin Tifou

sentences.zh: 李乂薛登韋湊從子虛心虛舟

translations.literal: Li Yi, Xue Deng, Wei Cou, and his nephews Xuxin and Xuzhou
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, Xue Deng, Wei Cou, and his nephews Xuxin and Xuzhou

sentences.zh: 韓思復曾孫佽

translations.literal: Han Sifu, and his great-grandson Ci
translations.idiomatic: Han Sifu, and his great-grandson Ci

sentences.zh: 張廷珪王求禮辛替否

translations.literal: Zhang Tinggui, Wang Qiuli, Xin Tifou
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui, Wang Qiuli, and Xin Tifou

sentences.zh: 李乂，本名尚真，趙州房子人也。

translations.literal: Li Yi, whose original name was Shangzhen, was a native of Fangzi in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, whose original name was Shangzhen, came from Fangzi in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少與兄尚一、尚貞俱以文章見稱，舉進士。

translations.literal: In his youth he and his elder brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were all famed for their literary talent and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he and his elder brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were all celebrated for their writing and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong period he rose through successive appointments to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時中宗遣使江南分道贖生，以所在官物充直。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhongzong dispatched envoys to the Jiangnan region by separate routes to redeem living creatures, using official goods from each locality as payment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Zhongzong sent envoys to the Jiangnan region by different routes to buy back living creatures, paying with official goods from each locality.

sentences.zh: 乂上疏曰：「江南水鄉，采捕為業，魚鱉之利，黎元所資，土地使然，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial, saying: "The Jiangnan is a land of rivers and lakes; catching and gathering is the people's occupation. The profit from fish and turtles is what the common folk rely upon—this is dictated by the land and has been so from old.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial, saying: "The Jiangnan is a country of rivers and lakes where people live by catching and gathering. Fish and turtles are the common people's livelihood—such is the land, and it has always been so.

sentences.zh: 伏以聖慈含育，恩周動植，布天下之大德，及鱗介之微品。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's compassionate nurturing extends its grace to all living and growing things, spreading great virtue throughout the realm even to the smallest creatures with scales and shells.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty's compassionate care embraces all living things, spreading great virtue across the realm even to the tiniest scaled creatures.

sentences.zh: 雖雲雨之私，有霑於末類；

translations.literal: Though the private blessing of rain and clouds may reach the lowest classes of beings;
translations.idiomatic: Though the private grace of rain and clouds may touch the lowliest creatures;

sentences.zh: 而生成之惠，未洽於平人。

translations.literal: the benefit of sustaining life has not yet reached ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: the blessing of sustaining life has not yet reached ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 江湖之饒，生育無限；

translations.literal: The abundance of rivers and lakes allows limitless reproduction;
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and lakes teem with life without limit;

sentences.zh: 府庫之用，支供易殫。

translations.literal: but the resources of the treasury are easily exhausted by disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: yet the treasury's resources are quickly depleted by such outlays.

sentences.zh: 費之若少，則所濟何成；

translations.literal: If the expenditure is small, then how much can be accomplished;
translations.idiomatic: If the spending is modest, little can actually be saved;

sentences.zh: 用之倘多，則常支有闕。

translations.literal: if the expenditure is large, then regular outlays will fall short.
translations.idiomatic: if it is lavish, regular expenditures will fall short.

sentences.zh: 在於拯物，豈若憂人。

translations.literal: When it comes to saving creatures, how does that compare with caring for people?
translations.idiomatic: When the choice is between saving creatures and caring for people, is the former truly the better course?

sentences.zh: 且鬻生之徒，唯利斯視，錢刀日至，網罟年滋，施之一朝，營之百倍，未若回救贖之錢物，減困貧之徭賦，活國愛人，其福勝彼。」

translations.literal: Moreover, those who trade in living things care only for profit; money comes in daily and nets multiply yearly. Give once and they profit a hundredfold. Better to turn the funds for redemption back, reduce corvée and taxes on the poor and distressed, revive the state and cherish the people—the blessing of that would surpass the other."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who sell living creatures care only for profit—coin arrives daily and nets grow year by year. A single day's bounty yields a hundredfold return. Better to redirect the redemption funds, lighten corvée and taxes on the poor and distressed, revive the state and cherish the people—the blessing would far exceed the other."

sentences.zh: 乂知制誥凡數載。

translations.literal: Yi drafted imperial edicts for several years in all.
translations.idiomatic: For several years Yi served as drafter of imperial proclamations.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，遷吏部侍郎，與宋璟、盧從願同時典選，銓敘平允，甚為當時所稱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; together with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan he concurrently managed selection, conducting appointments with fairness, and was greatly praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 he became Vice Minister of Personnel. He shared charge of appointments with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan, and their even-handed evaluations won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 尋轉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗令造金仙、玉真二觀，乂頻上疏諫，帝每優容之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ruizong ordered construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries; Yi repeatedly submitted memorials in remonstrance, and the emperor each time treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ordered the building of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries, Yi memorialized repeatedly in protest, and the emperor each time received him leniently.

sentences.zh: 開元初，特令乂與中書侍郎蘇颋纂集起居註，錄其嘉謨昌言可體國經遠者，別編奏之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was specially ordered, together with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Ting, to compile the Diaries of Activity and Repose, selecting excellent plans and splendid words fit to embody statecraft and guide the distant future, editing them separately and submitting them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he was specially assigned, with Secretariat Vice Minister Su Ting, to compile the court diaries, extract counsel and speeches that could serve long-range statecraft, and present them in a separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 乂在門下，多所駁正。

translations.literal: While Yi served in the Chancellery, he often rejected and corrected documents.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Chancellery, Yi frequently struck down or revised draft documents.

sentences.zh: 開元初，姚崇為紫微令，薦乂為紫微侍郎，外托薦賢，其實引在己下，去其糾駁之權也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan Yao Chong was Director of the Purple Tenuity Bureau; he recommended Yi as Vice Director, outwardly on the pretext of promoting the worthy, but in fact drawing him beneath himself and removing his power to criticize and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, when Yao Chong headed the Purple Tenuity Bureau, he recommended Yi as vice director—ostensibly to advance talent, but in truth to place him under his own authority and strip him of the power to review and reject.

sentences.zh: 俄拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 乂方雅有學識，朝廷稱其有宰相之望，會病卒。

translations.literal: Yi was refined and possessed learning; the court said he had the makings of a chief minister, but he happened to die of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and learned, Yi was spoken of at court as a man with the makings of a chief minister, but he died of illness before that could come to pass.

sentences.zh: 兄尚一，清源尉，早卒；

translations.literal: His elder brother Shangyi, magistrate of Qingyuan, died early;
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shangyi, magistrate of Qingyuan, died young;

sentences.zh: 尚貞，官至博州刺史。

translations.literal: Shangzhen rose to governor of Bo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhen rose to serve as governor of Bo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同為一集，號曰《李氏花萼集》，總二十卷。

translations.literal: The brothers jointly compiled one collection, entitled Collected Writings of the Li Brothers at the Flower Calyx Pavilion, twenty juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers jointly published a collection called the Li Brothers' Flower Calyx Anthology, twenty juan in all.

sentences.zh: 薛登，本名謙光，常州義興人也。

translations.literal: Xue Deng, whose original name was Qianguang, was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Deng, whose original name was Qianguang, came from Yixing in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父士通，大業中為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: His father Shitong served as Eagle-raising Commandant during the Daye era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shitong served as Eagle-raising Commandant during the Sui Daye period.

sentences.zh: 江都之亂，士通與鄉人聞人嗣安等同據本郡，以禦寇賊。

translations.literal: During the turmoil at Jiangdu, Shitong together with his fellow townsman Wenren Sian and others jointly held their home commandery to repel bandits and raiders.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval at Jiangdu, Shitong joined with his fellow townsman Wenren Sian and others in seizing control of their home commandery to defend against bandits.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，遣使歸國，高祖嘉之，降璽書勞勉，拜東武州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he sent envoys to submit to the new dynasty. Emperor Gaozu commended him, issued an imperial letter of praise and encouragement, and appointed him Prefect of Dongwu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 he sent envoys to submit to the new regime. Emperor Gaozu praised him, issued an imperial letter of commendation, and appointed him prefect of Dongwu.

sentences.zh: 俄而輔公祏於江都構逆，遣其將西門君儀等寇常州，士通率兵拒戰，大破之，君儀等僅以身免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Fu Gongshi raised rebellion at Jiangdu and sent his generals Ximen Junyi and others to raid Chang Prefecture. Shitong led troops to resist and inflicted a great defeat; Junyi and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fu Gongshi rebelled at Jiangdu and sent his generals Ximen Junyi and others to attack Chang Prefecture. Shitong led troops against them, won a great victory, and Junyi and his men barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 及公祏平，累功封臨汾侯。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi was pacified, Shitong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linfen for accumulated merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Gongshi was suppressed, Shitong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linfen for his accumulated achievements.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷遷泉州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was promoted through successive posts to Prefect of Quan Prefecture, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he rose through successive appointments to prefect of Quan Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 謙光博涉文史，每與人談論前代故事，必廣引證驗，有如目擊。

translations.literal: Qianguang was broadly versed in literature and history. Whenever he discussed past events with others, he would cite extensive evidence and verification as though he had witnessed them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qianguang was widely read in literature and history. Whenever he discussed events of earlier ages, he cited extensive evidence as though he had seen them with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 少與徐堅、劉子玄齊名友善。

translations.literal: In his youth he was equally famed and friendly with Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he enjoyed equal renown and close friendship with Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 文明中，解褐閬中主簿。

translations.literal: During the Wenming era he left the cloth and took office as Registrar of Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wenming period he entered official service as registrar of Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 天授中，為左補闕，時選舉頗濫，謙光上疏曰：

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he served as Left Remonstrator. At that time official selection was quite lax, and Qianguang submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou period he served as Left Remonstrator. At that time official appointments were quite indiscriminate, and Qianguang submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國以得賢為寶，臣以舉士為忠。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that a state treasures the gaining of worthy men, and that a minister shows loyalty by recommending scholars.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a state treasures the acquisition of worthy men, and that a minister proves his loyalty by recommending talent.

sentences.zh: 是以子皮之讓國僑，鮑叔之推管仲，燕昭委兵於樂毅，苻堅托政於王猛。

translations.literal: Thus Zipi yielded the state to Guo Qiao, Baoshu recommended Guan Zhong, King Zhao of Yan entrusted his army to Yue Yi, and Fu Jian entrusted governance to Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zipi yielded the state to Guo Qiao, Baoshu recommended Guan Zhong, King Zhao of Yan entrusted his armies to Yue Yi, and Fu Jian entrusted the government to Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 子產受國人之謗，夷吾貪共賈之財，昭王錫輅馬以止讒，永固戮樊世以除譖。

translations.literal: Zichan endured slander from the people of his state; Yiwu was greedy for the wealth of Gongjia; King Zhao bestowed carriage horses to stop slander; Yonggu executed Fan Shi to remove calumny.
translations.idiomatic: Zichan endured slander from his countrymen; Yiwu was greedy for Gongjia's wealth; King Zhao bestowed carriage horses to silence slander; Yonggu executed Fan Shi to remove calumny.

sentences.zh: 處猜嫌而益信，行間毀而無疑，此由默而識之，委而察之深也。

translations.literal: They stood amid suspicion yet gained greater trust; they acted amid slander yet remained unquestioned—this was because their rulers understood them in silence and entrusted them with deep discernment.
translations.idiomatic: They stood amid suspicion yet won greater trust; they moved amid slander yet remained unquestioned—because their rulers understood them in silence and entrusted them with deep insight.

sentences.zh: 至若宰我見愚於宣尼，逢萌被知於文叔，韓信無聞於項氏，毛遂不齒於平原，此失士之故也。

translations.literal: As for Zai Wo, who was deemed foolish by Confucius; Feng Meng, who was recognized by Emperor Guangwu; Han Xin, who went unnoticed by Xiang Yu; and Mao Sui, who was not ranked among Lord Pingyuan's retainers—these are cases of losing worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Zai Wo, deemed foolish by Confucius; Feng Meng, recognized by Emperor Guangwu; Han Xin, overlooked by Xiang Yu; and Mao Sui, not counted among Lord Pingyuan's retainers—these are cases of losing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 是以人主受不肖之士則政乖，得賢良之佐則時泰，故堯資八元而庶績其理，周任十亂而天下和平。

translations.literal: Thus when a ruler employs unworthy men, governance goes awry; when he gains worthy and good assistants, the age flourishes. Therefore Yao relied on the Eight Worthies and all affairs were well ordered; Zhou employed the Ten Disordered Ones and the realm was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler employs unworthy men, governance goes awry; when he gains worthy assistants, the age flourishes. Yao relied on the Eight Worthies and all affairs were well ordered; Zhou employed the Ten Disordered Ones and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，則士不可不察，而官不可妄授也。

translations.literal: From this it follows that scholars must not go unexamined, and offices must not be recklessly granted.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that scholars must be carefully scrutinized and offices must not be awarded indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 比來舉薦，多不以才，假譽馳聲，互相推獎，希潤身之小計，忘臣子之大猷，非所以報國求賢，副陛下翹翹之望者也。

translations.literal: In recent times recommendations have largely not been based on talent; with borrowed repute and inflated fame, people mutually promote and extol one another, hoping for petty plans to enrich themselves, forgetting the great design of minister and subject—this is not the way to serve the state and seek the worthy, nor to fulfill Your Majesty's lofty expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Recently most recommendations have been based not on talent but on borrowed reputations and inflated fame, with mutual puffery and promotion. Men aim at petty self-advancement and forget the great duty of minister and subject. This is no way to serve the state, seek worthy men, or fulfill Your Majesty's lofty expectations.

sentences.zh: 臣竊窺古之取士，實異於今。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to observe that the selection of scholars in antiquity was truly different from today.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to observe that how ancient rulers chose scholars was very different from today.

sentences.zh: 先觀名行之源，考其鄉邑之譽，崇禮讓以勵己，明節義以標信，以敦樸為先最，以雕蟲為後科。

translations.literal: They first looked to the source of one's reputation and conduct, examined one's standing in one's native district, honored courtesy and deference to encourage oneself, made integrity and righteousness clear as marks of trustworthiness, regarded plain sincerity as the foremost criterion, and treated ornamental writing as a secondary qualification.
translations.idiomatic: They first traced the origins of a man's reputation and character, weighed his standing in his home district, upheld courtesy and deference as self-discipline, and held up integrity and righteousness as proof of trustworthiness. Plain sincerity came first; ornamental composition came last.

sentences.zh: 故人崇勸讓之風，士去輕浮之行。

translations.literal: Thus people honored the spirit of urging one another toward deference, and scholars cast off frivolous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people valued the spirit of mutual encouragement and deference, and scholars shunned frivolous behavior.

sentences.zh: 希仕者必修貞確不拔之操，行難進易退之規。

translations.literal: Those who hoped for office had to cultivate steadfast integrity that could not be uprooted, and follow the principle of finding it hard to advance but easy to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought office had to cultivate steadfast integrity and abide by the principle that one should find it hard to accept advancement yet easy to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 眾議以定其高下，郡將難誣於曲直。

translations.literal: Public discussion determined their rank, and prefects could not misrepresent matters of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Public consensus fixed their standing, and prefects could not distort matters of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 故計貢之賢愚，即州將之榮辱；

translations.literal: Thus the wisdom or folly of tribute candidates reflected directly on the honor or disgrace of the prefect;
translations.idiomatic: The merit or folly of those recommended reflected directly on the prefect's own honor or shame;

sentences.zh: 穢行之彰露，亦鄉人之厚顏。

translations.literal: when base conduct was exposed, it was also a source of shame for the people of the district.
translations.idiomatic: when disgraceful conduct came to light, it shamed the people of the district as well.

sentences.zh: 是以李陵降而隴西慚，幹木隱而西河美。

translations.literal: Thus when Li Ling surrendered, Longxi was ashamed; when Gan Mu lived in seclusion, Xihe was honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ling surrendered, Longxi was shamed; when Gan Mu lived in seclusion, Xihe took pride in him.

sentences.zh: 故名勝於利，則小人之道消；

translations.literal: When reputation prevailed over profit, the way of petty men vanished;
translations.idiomatic: When reputation outweighed profit, the ways of petty men faded;

sentences.zh: 利勝於名，則貪暴之風扇。

translations.literal: when profit prevailed over reputation, the wind of greed and violence fanned up.
translations.idiomatic: when profit beat out reputation, greed and violence spread.

sentences.zh: 是以化俗之本，須擯輕浮。

translations.literal: Thus the foundation of transforming custom must reject frivolity.
translations.idiomatic: The root of reforming custom lies in rejecting frivolity.

sentences.zh: 昔冀缺以禮讓升朝，則晉人知禮；

translations.literal: Formerly Jique ascended to court through courtesy and deference, and the people of Jin understood propriety;
translations.idiomatic: Once Jique entered court through courtesy and deference, and the people of Jin learned what ritual meant;

sentences.zh: 文翁以儒林獎俗，則蜀士多儒。

translations.literal: Wen Weng rewarded custom through the Confucian grove, and the scholars of Shu became many in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Weng cultivated learning through the Confucian schools, and Shu produced many true scholars.

sentences.zh: 燕昭好馬，則駿馬來庭；

translations.literal: King Zhao of Yan loved horses, and fine steeds came to his court;
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Yan loved horses, and fine steeds came to his court;

sentences.zh: 葉公好龍，則真龍入室。

translations.literal: Lord Ye loved dragons, and a real dragon entered his hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Ye loved dragons, and a real dragon came into his hall.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，未有上之所好而下不從其化者也。

translations.literal: From this it follows that there has never been a case where those above had a preference and those below did not follow its transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the people below never fail to follow the taste set by those above.

sentences.zh: 自七國之季，雖雜縱橫，而漢代求才，猶征百行。

translations.literal: From the age of the Seven States, though the horizontal and vertical schools mixed, the Han in seeking talent still sought evidence in all aspects of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the late Warring States, when diplomatic strategists abounded, the Han still sought talent across every field of conduct.

sentences.zh: 是以禮節之士，敏德自修，閭裏推高，然後為府寺所辟。

translations.literal: Thus men of ritual propriety diligently cultivated virtue, were exalted in their neighborhoods, and only then were summoned by prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: Men of propriety diligently cultivated virtue, won esteem in their neighborhoods, and only then received summons from local offices.

sentences.zh: 魏氏取人，尤愛放達；

translations.literal: The Wei in selecting men especially favored free and unrestrained spirit;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei dynasty in choosing men especially favored free-spirited unconventionality;

sentences.zh: 晉、宋之後，祗重門資。

translations.literal: After Jin and Song, they valued only family status.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin and Song, they valued only family pedigree.

sentences.zh: 獎為人求官之風，乖授職惟賢之義。

translations.literal: They rewarded the practice of seeking office for others, contrary to the principle of appointing only the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: They encouraged the custom of pulling strings for office, betraying the principle of appointing the worthy alone.

sentences.zh: 有梁薦士，雅愛屬詞；

translations.literal: Liang in recommending scholars especially loved literary composition;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang prized literary composition when recommending scholars;

sentences.zh: 陳氏簡賢，特珍賦詠。

translations.literal: Chen in selecting the worthy especially treasured poetic composition.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen, in screening talent, prized poetry above all else.

sentences.zh: 故其俗以詩酒為重，不以修身為務。

translations.literal: Thus their custom valued poetry and wine, and did not make self-cultivation its task.
translations.idiomatic: Thus their society prized poetry and wine and did not make self-cultivation its aim.

sentences.zh: 逮至隋室，餘風尚在，開皇中李諤論之於文帝曰：「魏之三祖，更好文詞，忽君人之大道，好雕蟲之小藝。

translations.literal: By the time of the Sui, the lingering influence remained. During Kaihuang, Li E argued before Emperor Wen, saying: "The three founders of Wei all the more favored literary composition, neglecting the great Way of ruler and people, and loving the petty craft of ornamental writing.
translations.idiomatic: By the Sui dynasty that lingering taste still held. During Kaihuang, Li E argued before Emperor Wen, saying: "The three founders of Wei favored literary composition all the more, neglecting the great Way of rulership and forgetting the people, while cherishing the petty craft of ornamental writing.

sentences.zh: 連篇累牘，不出月露之形；

translations.literal: Essay piled upon essay never went beyond the shapes of moon and dew;
translations.idiomatic: Essay piled upon essay never rose above descriptions of moonlight and dew;

sentences.zh: 積案盈箱，唯是風雲之狀。

translations.literal: Documents filled cases and chests, containing only images of wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Documents filled desks and chests with nothing but images of wind and clouds.

sentences.zh: 代俗以此相高，朝廷以茲擢士，故文筆日煩，其政日亂」。

translations.literal: The age's custom took this as a mark of elevation, and the court used it to promote scholars; thus literary composition grew daily more burdensome, and governance daily more chaotic."
translations.idiomatic: The age took this as a mark of distinction, and the court used it to promote scholars; thus literary composition grew ever more burdensome, and governance ever more chaotic."

sentences.zh: 帝納李諤之策，由是下制禁斷文筆浮詞。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted Li E's proposal, and thereupon issued an edict forbidding ornamental and empty literary language.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted Li E's proposal and issued an edict forbidding ornamental and empty literary language.

sentences.zh: 其年，泗洲刺史司馬幼之以表不典實得罪。

translations.literal: That same year, Sima Youzhi, Prefect of Si Prefecture, was punished because his memorial was not canonical and factual.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Sima Youzhi, prefect of Si Prefecture, was punished because his memorial was uncanonical and insubstantial.

sentences.zh: 於是風俗改勵，政化大行。

translations.literal: Thereupon custom was reformed and invigorated, and governance and transformation were broadly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon custom was reformed and invigorated, and good governance spread widely.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣興，又變前法，置進士等科。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to power, he again changed the former law and established the jinshi and other examination categories.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he changed the former law again and established the jinshi and other examination categories.

sentences.zh: 於是後生之徒，復相放效，因陋就寡，赴速邀時，緝綴小文，名之策學，不以指實為本，而以浮虛為貴。

translations.literal: Thereupon the younger generation again imitated one another, clinging to the crude and meager, rushing for speed to seize the moment, stitching together small compositions called policy essays, taking substance as their foundation not, but holding emptiness and ornament dear.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the younger generation imitated one another again, clinging to the crude and shallow, rushing to seize the moment, stitching together small compositions called policy essays—not grounding themselves in substance, but prizing emptiness and ornament.

sentences.zh: 有唐纂歷，雖漸革於故非；

translations.literal: The Tang has received the mandate and, though it has gradually reformed former abuses;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang has received the mandate and, though it has gradually reformed former abuses;

sentences.zh: 陛下君臨，思察才於共理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty rules the realm and seeks to discern talent in shared governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules the realm and seeks to discern talent for shared governance.

sentences.zh: 樹本崇化，惟在旌賢。

translations.literal: To plant the root and exalt transformation lies solely in honoring the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: To lay a firm foundation and elevate the realm lies solely in honoring the worthy.

sentences.zh: 今之舉人，有乖事實。

translations.literal: Today's examination candidates depart from the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Today's examination candidates depart from the facts.

sentences.zh: 鄉議決小人之筆，行修無長者之論。

translations.literal: District evaluations are decided by the pens of petty men, and conduct assessments lack the judgment of elders.
translations.idiomatic: District evaluations are decided by the pens of petty men, and conduct assessments lack the judgment of elders.

sentences.zh: 策第喧競於州府，祈恩不勝於拜伏。

translations.literal: Examination rankings clamor and compete at prefectural offices, and pleading for favor is surpassed only by prostration.
translations.idiomatic: Examination rankings are fought over noisily at prefectural offices, and pleading for favor gives way to outright prostration.

sentences.zh: 或明制才出，試遣搜敭，驅馳府寺之門，出入王公之第。

translations.literal: Sometimes as soon as the regulations were issued, testing envoys were dispatched to search and review, rushing to the gates of prefectural offices and going in and out of princes' mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes no sooner were the regulations promulgated than examination envoys were sent out to search and review candidates, rushing to the gates of prefectural offices and passing in and out of princes' mansions.

sentences.zh: 上啟陳詩，唯希咳唾之澤；

translations.literal: They submit memorials and present poems, hoping only for the bounty of a patron's spittle;
translations.idiomatic: They submit memorials and present poems, hoping only for the crumbs of a patron's favor;

sentences.zh: 摩頂至足，冀荷提攜之恩。

translations.literal: from crown to sole they abase themselves, hoping to receive the grace of being lifted up.
translations.idiomatic: from head to foot they abase themselves, hoping to receive the grace of being lifted up.

sentences.zh: 故俗號舉人，皆稱覓舉。

translations.literal: Thus by custom those called examination candidates are all termed seekers of recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus by custom those called examination candidates are all termed seekers of recommendation.

sentences.zh: 覓為自求之稱，未是人知之辭。

translations.literal: Seeking is a term for self-advancement, not language for others recognizing one's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking is a term for self-advancement, not language for others recognizing one's merit.

sentences.zh: 察其行而度其材，則人品於茲見矣。

translations.literal: Examine their conduct and measure their talent, and a man's character is seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: Examine their conduct and measure their talent, and a man's character becomes plain.

sentences.zh: 徇己之心切，則至公之理乖；

translations.literal: When the heart bent on self-interest is keen, then the principle of utmost fairness is violated;
translations.idiomatic: When self-interest runs strong, the principle of utmost fairness is violated;

sentences.zh: 貪仕之性彰，則廉潔之風薄。

translations.literal: when the nature greedy for office is displayed, then the wind of integrity grows thin.
translations.idiomatic: when greed for office shows itself, the spirit of integrity grows thin.

sentences.zh: 是知府命雖高，異叔度勤勤之讓；

translations.literal: From this one knows that though a prefectural appointment is lofty, it differs from Shudu's repeated and earnest declinations;
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that though a prefectural appointment is lofty, it is nothing like Shudu's repeated and earnest declinations;

sentences.zh: 黃門已貴，無秦嘉耿耿之辭。

translations.literal: though the Yellow Gate is already exalted, there is none of Qin Jia's solemn and earnest language.
translations.idiomatic: though the Yellow Gate is already exalted, there is none of Qin Jia's solemn and earnest language.

sentences.zh: 縱不能抑己推賢，亦不肯待於三命。

translations.literal: Even if they cannot restrain themselves and recommend the worthy, they are also unwilling to wait for the third summons.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they cannot restrain themselves and recommend the worthy, they are unwilling to wait for the third summons.

sentences.zh: 豈與夫白駒皎皎，不雜風塵，束帛戔戔，榮高物表，校量其廣狹也！

translations.literal: How can this compare with the white colt, bright and unsullied by worldly dust, or with silken gifts in abundance and honor transcending worldly things—how wide is the gap between them!
translations.idiomatic: How can this compare with the white colt, bright and unsullied by worldly dust, or with abundant silken gifts and honor transcending the common world—how vast is the distance between them!

sentences.zh: 是以耿介之士，羞自拔而致其辭；

translations.literal: Thus upright and principled men are ashamed to promote themselves and offer their words;
translations.idiomatic: Thus upright men are ashamed to promote themselves and offer their words;

sentences.zh: 循常之人，舍其疏而取其附。

translations.literal: ordinary men discard those who keep their distance and take those who attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: ordinary men discard those who keep their distance and take those who attach themselves.

sentences.zh: 故選司補署，喧然於禮闈；

translations.literal: Thus the selection office's appointments resound noisily in the examination hall;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the selection office's appointments resound noisily in the examination hall;

sentences.zh: 州貢賓王，爭訟於階闥。

translations.literal: prefectural tribute candidates dispute at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: prefectural tribute candidates dispute at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 謗議紛合，浸以成風。

translations.literal: Slander and debate gather in confusion and gradually become custom.
translations.idiomatic: Slander and dispute gather in confusion and gradually become custom.

sentences.zh: 夫競榮者必有競利之心，謙遜者亦無貪賄之累。

translations.literal: Those who compete for glory necessarily have hearts that compete for profit; the modest and deferential are also free from the burden of greedy bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Those who compete for glory necessarily compete for profit as well; the modest and deferential are free from the taint of bribery.

sentences.zh: 自非上智，焉能不移；

translations.literal: Unless one is of the highest wisdom, how can one remain unmoved;
translations.idiomatic: Unless one is of the highest wisdom, how can one remain unmoved;

sentences.zh: 在於中人，理由習俗。

translations.literal: for ordinary men, reason lies in custom.
translations.idiomatic: for ordinary men, conduct follows custom.

sentences.zh: 若重謹厚之士，則懷祿者必崇德以修名；

translations.literal: If prudent and sincere men are honored, then those who hold office will necessarily exalt virtue to cultivate their reputation;
translations.idiomatic: If prudent and sincere men are honored, then officeholders will exalt virtue to cultivate their reputation;

sentences.zh: 若開趨競之門，邀仕者皆戚施而附會。

translations.literal: if the gate of rushing competition is opened, those who seek office will all be hunchbacks who attach and flatter.
translations.idiomatic: if the gate of rushing competition is opened, those who seek office will all bow and scrape in flattery.

sentences.zh: 附會則百姓罹其弊，潔己則兆庶蒙其福。

translations.literal: When there is flattery and attachment, the common people suffer its harm; when one keeps oneself pure, the multitude receive its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: When there is flattery and attachment, the common people suffer; when one keeps oneself pure, the multitude receive the blessing.

sentences.zh: 故風化之漸，靡不由茲。

translations.literal: Thus the gradual progress of transformation and instruction—none does not proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the gradual transformation of custom proceeds entirely from this.

sentences.zh: 今訪鄉閭之談，唯祇歸於裏正。

translations.literal: Now in inquiring into village gossip, it all comes down solely to the village head.
translations.idiomatic: Now when one inquires into village gossip, everything comes down solely to the village head.

sentences.zh: 縱使名虧禮則，罪掛刑章，或冒籍以偷資，或邀勛而竊級，假其不義之賂，則是無犯鄉閭。

translations.literal: Even if one's reputation falls short of ritual propriety and guilt is recorded in the penal code—even if one falsely registers to steal qualifications, or seeks merit to seize rank—as long as improper bribes are given, then one has not offended the village.
translations.idiomatic: Even if reputation falls short of propriety and guilt hangs in the penal code—even if one falsely registers to steal qualifications, or trades on merit to seize rank—as long as improper bribes are paid, one has not offended the village.

sentences.zh: 豈得比郭有道之銓量，茅容望重，裴逸人之賞拔，夏少名高，語其優劣也！

translations.literal: How can this compare with Guo Youdao's balanced evaluation, Mao Rong's heavy repute, Pei Yiren's discerning promotion, and Xia Shao's lofty fame, when speaking of superiority and inferiority!
translations.idiomatic: How can this compare with Guo Tai's measured judgment, Mao Rong's great standing, Pei Xia's discerning promotion, and Xia Shao's lofty fame, when one speaks of who is better and who worse!

sentences.zh: 祇如才應經邦之流，唯令試策；

translations.literal: Take for example those whose talent suits governing the state—they are made to take only the written examination;
translations.idiomatic: Take those whose talent suits governing the state—they are made to take only the written examination;

sentences.zh: 武能制敵之例，只驗彎弧。

translations.literal: for those whose martial skill can subdue enemies, only bending the bow is tested.
translations.idiomatic: for those whose martial skill can subdue enemies, only bending the bow is tested.

sentences.zh: 若其文擅清奇，便充甲第，藻思微減，便即告歸。

translations.literal: If their writing excels in clarity and originality, they are placed in the top rank; if literary thought is slightly diminished, they are immediately sent home.
translations.idiomatic: If their writing excels in clarity and originality, they are placed in the top rank; if literary thought is slightly diminished, they are sent home at once.

sentences.zh: 以此收人，恐乖事實。

translations.literal: To select men by this method fears departing from the facts.
translations.idiomatic: To select men in this way would surely depart from the facts.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 樂廣假筆於潘嶽，靈運詞高於穆之，平津文劣於長卿，子建筆麗於荀彧。

translations.literal: Yue Guang borrowed Pan Yue's brush; Lingyun's words were loftier than Muyi's; the Marquis of Pingjin's writing was inferior to Xiangru's; Zijian's brush was finer than Xun Yu's.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guang borrowed Pan Yue's brush; Xie Lingyun's words were loftier than Xu Muyi's; the Marquis of Pingjin's writing was inferior to Sima Xiangru's; Cao Zhi's brush was finer than Xun Yu's.

sentences.zh: 若以射策為最，則潘、謝、曹、馬必居孫、樂之右；

translations.literal: If written examinations were supreme, then Pan, Xie, Cao, and Ma would necessarily rank above Sun and Yue;
translations.idiomatic: If written examinations were supreme, then Pan, Xie, Cao, and Ma would necessarily rank above Sun and Yue;

sentences.zh: 若使協贊機猷，則安仁、靈運亦無裨附之益。

translations.literal: If they were made to assist in planning strategy, then Anren and Lingyun would also be of no supplementary benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If they were made to assist in planning strategy, then Pan Anren and Xie Lingyun would also be of no real benefit.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，不可一概而取也。

translations.literal: From this perspective, one cannot apply a single standard in selection.
translations.idiomatic: From this perspective, one cannot apply a single standard in selection.

sentences.zh: 至如武藝，則趙雲雖勇，資諸葛之指捴；

translations.literal: As for martial arts, though Zhao Yun was brave, he relied on Zhuge's command;
translations.idiomatic: As for martial skill, though Zhao Yun was brave, he relied on Zhuge Liang's direction;

sentences.zh: 周勃雖雄，乏陳平之計略。

translations.literal: though Zhou Bo was heroic, he lacked Chen Ping's stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: though Zhou Bo was heroic, he lacked Chen Ping's stratagems.

sentences.zh: 若使樊噲居蕭何之任，必失指縱之機；

translations.literal: If Fan Kuai held Xiao He's office, he would surely miss the moment for command and control;
translations.idiomatic: If Fan Kuai held Xiao He's office, he would surely miss the moment for command and control;

sentences.zh: 使蕭何入戲下之軍，亦無免主之效。

translations.literal: if Xiao He entered the army beneath the commander's tent, he would also have no effect of saving his lord.
translations.idiomatic: if Xiao He entered the army beneath the commander's tent, he would also have no power to save his lord.

sentences.zh: 鬥將長於摧鋒，謀將審於料事。

translations.literal: Fighting generals excel at breaking the enemy vanguard; plotting generals are careful in anticipating affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting generals excel at breaking the enemy vanguard; plotting generals are careful in anticipating affairs.

sentences.zh: 是以文泉聚米，知隗囂之可圖；

translations.literal: Thus Wen Yuan piled rice [into a map] and knew Wei Xiao's realm could be taken;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wen Yuan piled rice into a map and knew that Wei Xiao's realm could be taken;

sentences.zh: 陳湯屈指，識烏孫之自解。

translations.literal: Chen Tang counted on his fingers and recognized that the Wusun would resolve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang counted on his fingers and recognized that the Wusun would resolve the matter themselves.

sentences.zh: 八難之謀設，高祖追慚於酈生；

translations.literal: When the eight-difficulties stratagem was devised, Emperor Gaozu felt remorse toward Li Yiji;
translations.idiomatic: When the eight-difficulties stratagem was devised, Emperor Gaozu felt remorse toward Li Yiji;

sentences.zh: 九拒之計窮，公輸息心於伐宋。

translations.literal: when the nine-refusals stratagem was exhausted, Gongshu ceased his intention of attacking Song.
translations.idiomatic: when the nine-refusals stratagem was exhausted, Gongshu Ban abandoned his plan to attack Song.

sentences.zh: 謀將不長於弓馬，良相寧資於射策。

translations.literal: Plotting generals do not excel at bow and horse; fine ministers surely need not rely on written examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Plotting generals do not excel at bow and horse; fine ministers need not rely on written examinations.

sentences.zh: 豈與夫元長自表，妄飾詞鋒，曹植題章，虛飛麗藻，校量其可否也！

translations.literal: How is this comparable to Yuan Chang's self-recommendation, falsely polishing verbal edge, or Cao Zhi's submitted memorial, vainly flying with ornate prose—weighing whether they pass muster!
translations.idiomatic: How is this comparable to Yuan Chang's self-recommendation, falsely polishing his rhetoric, or Cao Zhi's submitted memorial, vainly flying with ornate prose—weighing whether they pass muster!

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下降明制，頒峻科。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will issue enlightened regulations and promulgate strict standards.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will issue enlightened regulations and promulgate strict standards.

sentences.zh: 千里一賢，尚不為少，僥幸冒進，須立堤防。

translations.literal: One worthy man in a thousand miles is still no small number; opportunistic rushing forward must have dikes built against it.
translations.idiomatic: One worthy man in a thousand miles is still no small number; opportunistic rushing forward must be held back by firm barriers.

sentences.zh: 斷浮虛之飾詞，收實用之良策，不取無稽之說，必求忠告之言。

translations.literal: Cut off empty and false ornamental language; gather practical and effective policies; do not accept baseless talk; one must seek words of sincere admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off empty and ornamental language; gather practical and effective policies; do not accept baseless talk; seek words of sincere admonition.

sentences.zh: 文則試以效官，武則令其守禦，始既察言觀行，終亦循名責實，自然僥幸濫吹之伍，無所藏其妄庸。

translations.literal: For civil talent, test them by performance in office; for military talent, have them defend and guard; at first observe words and examine conduct, and in the end match names to reality—then naturally the crowd of opportunists and inflated impostors will have nowhere to hide their empty mediocrity.
translations.idiomatic: For civil talent, test them by performance in office; for military talent, have them defend and guard; at first observe words and examine conduct, and in the end match names to reality—then naturally the crowd of opportunists and inflated impostors will have nowhere to hide their empty mediocrity.

sentences.zh: 故晏嬰云：「舉之以語，考之以事；

translations.literal: Therefore Yan Ying said: "Raise them by their words, examine them by their deeds;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yan Ying said: "Raise them by their words, examine them by their deeds;

sentences.zh: 寡其言而多其行，拙於文而工於事。」

translations.literal: few in speech but abundant in action, clumsy in letters but skilled in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: few in speech but abundant in action, clumsy in letters but skilled in affairs."

sentences.zh: 此取人得賢之道也。

translations.literal: This is the way of selecting men and obtaining the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: This is the way of selecting men and obtaining the worthy.

sentences.zh: 其有武藝超絕，文鋒挺秀，有效伎之偏用，無經國之大才，為軍鋒之爪牙，作詞賦之標準。

translations.literal: There are those whose martial skill is transcendent or whose literary edge stands out, who have special uses for particular skills but lack great talent for governing the state—they may serve as claws and fangs in the army's vanguard, or as standards in composing rhapsodies and prose.
translations.idiomatic: There are those whose martial skill is transcendent or whose literary edge stands out, who have special uses for particular skills but lack great talent for governing the state—they may serve as claws and fangs in the army's vanguard, or as models in composing rhapsodies and prose.

sentences.zh: 自可試淩雲之策，練穿劄之工，承上命而賦《甘泉》，稟中軍而令赴敵，既有隨才之任，必無負乘之憂。

translations.literal: They may be tested with cloud-scaling compositions, trained in pierced-target archery, receive the throne's command to compose the "Sweet Springs" rhapsody, or take orders from the central army and be sent against the enemy—when each is assigned according to talent, there will surely be no worry of the wrong man in the wrong seat.
translations.idiomatic: They may be tested with cloud-scaling compositions, trained in pierced-target archery, receive the throne's command to compose the "Sweet Springs" rhapsody, or take orders from the central army and be sent against the enemy—when each is assigned according to talent, there will be no worry of the wrong man in the wrong seat.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案吳起臨戰，左右進劍，吳子曰：「夫提鼓揮桴，臨難決疑，此將事也。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes: When Wu Qi faced battle, attendants brought him swords. Master Wu said: "Beating the drum and waving the mace, facing difficulty and resolving doubts—this is a general's business.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully notes: When Wu Qi faced battle, attendants brought him swords. Master Wu said: "Beating the drum and waving the mace, facing difficulty and resolving doubts—this is a general's business.

sentences.zh: 一劍之任，非將事也。」

translations.literal: The business of a single sword is not a general's business."
translations.idiomatic: The business of a single sword is not a general's business."

sentences.zh: 謹案諸葛亮臨戎，不親戎服，頓蜀兵於渭南，宣王持劍，卒不敢當。

translations.literal: Your subject notes: When Zhuge Liang faced war, he did not personally wear military dress; he stationed the Shu army on the south bank of the Wei River, and the Prince of Xuan held his sword yet in the end did not dare confront him.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject notes: When Zhuge Liang faced war, he did not personally wear military dress; he stationed the Shu army on the south bank of the Wei River, and Sima Yi held his sword yet in the end did not dare confront him.

sentences.zh: 此豈弓矢之用也！

translations.literal: Is this a matter of bow and arrow!
translations.idiomatic: Is this a matter of bow and arrow!

sentences.zh: 謹案楊得意誦長卿之文，武帝曰：「恨不得與此人同時。」

translations.literal: Your subject notes: When Yang Dedec recited Changqing's writing, Emperor Wu said: "I regret that I cannot be contemporary with this man."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject notes: When Yang Dedec recited Sima Xiangru's writing, Emperor Wu said: "I regret that I cannot be contemporary with this man."

sentences.zh: 及相如至，終於文園令，不以公卿之位處之者，蓋非其所任故也。

translations.literal: When Xiangru arrived, he ended as Warden of the Wen Garden—the reason he was not placed in ministerial rank was that such a position was not what he was suited for.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangru arrived, he ended as Warden of the Wen Garden—the reason he was not placed in ministerial rank was that such a position was not what he was suited for.

sentences.zh: 謹案漢法，所舉之主，終身保任。

translations.literal: Your subject notes: Under Han law, one who recommends others is responsible for them for life.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject notes: Under Han law, one who recommends others is responsible for them for life.

sentences.zh: 楊雄之坐田儀，責其冒薦；

translations.literal: Yang Xiong was implicated because of Tian Yi, held accountable for reckless recommendation;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong was implicated because of Tian Yi, held accountable for reckless recommendation;

sentences.zh: 成子之居魏相，酬於得賢。

translations.literal: when Cheng Xi served as Chancellor of Wei, he was rewarded for obtaining the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: when Cheng Xi served as Chancellor of Wei, he was rewarded for obtaining the worthy.

sentences.zh: 賞罰之令行，則請謁之心絕；

translations.literal: When reward and punishment orders are enforced, the heart that seeks favors through petitions is cut off;
translations.idiomatic: When reward and punishment orders are enforced, the heart that seeks favors through petitions is cut off;

sentences.zh: 退讓之義著，則貪競之路消。

translations.literal: when the principle of yielding and deferring is established, the path of greedy competition disappears.
translations.idiomatic: when the principle of yielding and deferring is established, the path of greedy competition disappears.

sentences.zh: 自然朝廷無爭祿之人，選司有謙捴之士。

translations.literal: Naturally the court will have no men contending for salaries, and the selection office will have modest and deferential men.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally the court will have no men contending for salaries, and the selection office will have modest and deferential men.

sentences.zh: 仍請寬立年限，容其采訪簡汰，堪用者令其試守，以觀能否；

translations.literal: I further ask that a generous time limit be set, allowing inquiry and selection to proceed; those who prove capable should be given probationary appointment to observe their ability;
translations.idiomatic: I further ask that a generous time limit be set, allowing inquiry and selection to proceed; those who prove capable should be given probationary appointment to observe their ability;

sentences.zh: 參驗行事，以別是非。

translations.literal: verify them by their conduct in office to distinguish right from wrong.
translations.idiomatic: verify them by their conduct in office to distinguish right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 不實免王丹之官，得人加翟璜之賞，自然見賢不隱，食祿不專。

translations.literal: If they prove unworthy, dismiss them as Wang Dan was dismissed; if worthy men are found, add rewards as Zhai Huang received—then naturally seeing the worthy one will not conceal them, and holding salary will not be monopolized.
translations.idiomatic: If they prove unworthy, dismiss them as Wang Dan was dismissed; if worthy men are found, add rewards as Zhai Huang received—then naturally seeing the worthy one will not conceal them, and holding salary will not be monopolized.

sentences.zh: 荀彧進鐘繇、郭嘉，劉隱薦李膺、硃穆，勢不雲遠。

translations.literal: Xun Yu promoted Zhong Yao and Guo Jia; Liu Wei recommended Li Ying and Zhu Mu—the precedent is not far to seek.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu promoted Zhong Yao and Guo Jia; Liu Wei recommended Li Ying and Zhu Mu—the precedent is not far to seek.

sentences.zh: 有稱職者受薦賢之賞，濫舉者抵欺罔之罪，自然舉得賢行，則君子之道長矣。

translations.literal: When those who perform capably receive reward for recommending the worthy, and reckless recommenders suffer punishment for deceit, then naturally when recommendations bring forth worthy conduct, the way of the superior man will flourish.
translations.idiomatic: When those who perform capably receive reward for recommending the worthy, and reckless recommenders suffer punishment for deceit, then naturally when recommendations bring forth worthy conduct, the way of the superior man will flourish.

sentences.zh: 尋轉水部員外郎，累遷給事中、檢校常州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Secretary for Waterways; through successive promotions he rose to Director within the Gates and Acting Prefect of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Secretary for Waterways; through successive promotions he rose to Director within the Gates and Acting Prefect of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬宣州狂寇硃大目作亂，百姓奔走，謙光嚴備安輯，闔境肅然。

translations.literal: When the rebel Zhu Daimu raised turmoil in Xuan Prefecture and the common people fled in panic, Qian'guang strictly prepared defenses and restored order, and the whole jurisdiction became calm.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Zhu Daimu raised turmoil in Xuan Prefecture and the common people fled in panic, Qian'guang strictly prepared defenses and restored order, and the whole jurisdiction became calm.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，再遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, given the Silver Seal and Blue-Girdle Grand Master of the Palace, and promoted again to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, given the Silver Seal and Blue-Girdle Grand Master of the Palace, and promoted again to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，擢拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he was promoted and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era he was promoted and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時僧惠範恃太平公主權勢，逼奪百姓店肆，州縣不能理。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Huifan relied on Princess Taiping's power to seize the shops of common people by force, and prefectures and counties could not address it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Huifan relied on Princess Taiping's power to seize the shops of common people by force, and prefectures and counties could not address it.

sentences.zh: 謙光將加彈奏，或請寢之，謙光曰：「憲臺理冤滯，何所回避，朝彈暮黜，亦可矣。」

translations.literal: When Qian'guang was about to impeach him, some urged him to drop the matter. Qian'guang said: "The censorate exists to resolve grievances and clear wrongs—what is there to evade? Impeached in the morning and dismissed by evening—that would be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: When Qian'guang was about to impeach him, some urged him to drop the matter. Qian'guang said: "The censorate exists to resolve grievances and clear wrongs—what is there to evade? Impeached in the morning and dismissed by evening—that would be acceptable."

sentences.zh: 遂與殿中慕容玽奏彈之，反為太平公主所構，出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he joined with Murong Ting of the Palace Attendants in submitting an impeachment, but was instead framed by Princess Taiping and sent out as Prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he joined with Murong Ting of the Palace Attendants in submitting an impeachment, but was instead framed by Princess Taiping and sent out as Prefect of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 惠範既誅，遷太子賓客，轉刑部尚書，加金紫光祿大夫、昭文館學士。

translations.literal: After Huifan was executed, he was moved to Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, transferred to Minister of Justice, and given the Gold Seal and Purple-Girdle Grand Master of the Palace and membership in the Zhaowen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Huifan was executed, he was moved to Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, transferred to Minister of Justice, and given the Gold Seal and Purple-Girdle Grand Master of the Palace and membership in the Zhaowen Academy.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為東都留守，又轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he served as Eastern Capital Regent, and was again transferred to Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he served as Eastern Capital Regent, and was again transferred to Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以與太子同名，表請行字，特敕賜名登。

translations.literal: Because he shared the given name with the Heir Apparent, he submitted a memorial requesting to use his style name; by special edict he was granted the name Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Because he shared the given name with the Heir Apparent, he submitted a memorial requesting to use his style name; by special edict he was granted the name Deng.

sentences.zh: 尋以孽子悅千牛為憲司所劾，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Soon because his illegitimate son Yue, a Thousand-Bull Cadet, was impeached by the censorate, he was dismissed and sent back to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Soon because his illegitimate son Yue, a Thousand-Bull Cadet, was impeached by the censorate, he was dismissed and sent back to his fields.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其家貧，又特給致仕祿。

translations.literal: Because his family was poor, the court specially granted him retirement salary.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family was poor, the court specially granted him retirement salary.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，年七十三，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year [of Kaiyuan], at age seventy-three, and was posthumously awarded the title of Prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year [of Kaiyuan], at age seventy-three, and was posthumously awarded the title of Prefect of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 撰《四時記》二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled the Records of the Four Seasons in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the Records of the Four Seasons in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 韋湊，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Cou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖瓚，隋尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zan was Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zan was Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 祖叔諧，蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuxie was Prefect of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuxie was Prefect of Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父玄，桂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was Chief Administrator of the Garrison Headquarters at Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was Chief Administrator of the Garrison Headquarters at Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 湊，永淳二年，解褐授婺州參軍，累轉揚府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Cou, in the second year of Yongchun, left his commoner's dress and was appointed Military Aide in Wu Prefecture; through successive promotions he became Legal Administrator in the Yangzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Cou, in the second year of Yongchun, left his commoner's dress and was appointed Military Aide in Wu Prefecture; through successive promotions he became Legal Administrator in the Yangzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 州人前仁壽令孟神爽豪縱，數犯法，交通貴戚，前後官吏莫敢繩按，湊白長史張潛，請因事除之。

translations.literal: A former magistrate of Renshou, Meng Shensuang, was overbearing and unrestrained, repeatedly breaking the law and associating with powerful kin; none of the officials before or after dared to investigate. Cou informed Chief Administrator Zhang Qian and asked to eliminate him when an opportunity arose.
translations.idiomatic: A former magistrate of Renshou, Meng Shensuang, was overbearing and unrestrained, repeatedly breaking the law and associating with powerful kin; none of the officials before or after dared to investigate. Cou informed Chief Administrator Zhang Qian and asked to eliminate him when an opportunity arose.

sentences.zh: 會神爽坐事推問，湊無所假借，神爽妄稱有密旨，究問引虛，遂杖殺之，遠近稱伏。

translations.literal: When Shensuang was implicated and brought for interrogation, Cou showed him no leniency; Shensuang falsely claimed there was a secret edict, and though the investigation proved this empty, Cou still had him beaten to death. Near and far praised and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Shensuang was implicated and brought for interrogation, Cou showed him no leniency; Shensuang falsely claimed there was a secret edict, and though the investigation proved this empty, Cou still had him beaten to death. Near and far praised and submitted.

sentences.zh: 湊，景龍中歷遷將作少匠、司農少卿。

translations.literal: Cou, in the Jinglong era, was promoted in succession to Assistant Master of Palace Construction and Vice Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cou, in the Jinglong era, was promoted in succession to Assistant Master of Palace Construction and Vice Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 嘗以公事忤宗楚客，出為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Once he offended Zong Chuke on official business and was sent out as Prefect of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once he offended Zong Chuke on official business and was sent out as Prefect of Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，拜鴻臚少卿，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Cou was appointed Vice Director of the Court for State Ceremonial and given the Silver Seal and Blue-Girdle Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Cou was appointed Vice Director of the Court for State Ceremonial and given the Silver Seal and Blue-Girdle Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，轉太府少卿，又兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Treasury and also served concurrently as Herald.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Treasury and also served concurrently as Herald.

sentences.zh: 時改葬節湣太子，優詔加謚；

translations.literal: At that time Prince Jiemin was being reburied, and an edict of favor added a posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Jiemin was being reburied, and an edict of favor added a posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 又雪李多祚等罪，還其官爵，仍議更加贈官。

translations.literal: the crimes of Li Duozuo and others were cleared, their offices and titles restored, and the court still deliberated on further posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: the crimes of Li Duozuo and others were cleared, their offices and titles restored, and the court still deliberated on further posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 湊上書曰：

translations.literal: Cou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞王者發號施令，必法乎天道，使三綱攸敘，十等鹹若者，善善明，惡惡著也。

translations.literal: I have heard that when a ruler issues commands and orders, he must take the Way of Heaven as his model, so that the three bonds are put in order and all ten ranks are thus settled—this is so that good is made clear for the good and evil is made manifest for the evil.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a ruler issues commands and orders, he must take the Way of Heaven as his model, so that the three bonds are put in order and all ten ranks are thus settled—this is so that good is made clear for the good and evil is made manifest for the evil.

sentences.zh: 善善者，懸爵賞以勸之也；

translations.literal: For the good, rank and reward are displayed to encourage them;
translations.idiomatic: For the good, rank and reward are displayed to encourage them;

sentences.zh: 惡惡者，設刑罰以懲之也。

translations.literal: for the evil, punishments are established to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: for the evil, punishments are established to chastise them.

sentences.zh: 其賞罰所不加者，則考行立謚以褒貶之，所以勸誡將來也。

translations.literal: What reward and punishment cannot reach is judged by conduct and given a posthumous title for praise or blame—this is to admonish those yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: What reward and punishment cannot reach is judged by conduct and given a posthumous title for praise or blame—this is to admonish those yet to come.

sentences.zh: 斯並至公之大猷，非私情之可徇。

translations.literal: All these are great principles of utmost fairness, not matters in which private feeling may be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: All these are great principles of utmost fairness, not matters in which private feeling may be indulged.

sentences.zh: 故箕、微獲用，管、蔡為戮。

translations.literal: Thus Jizi and Weizi were employed, while Guan and Cai were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jizi and Weizi were employed, while Guan and Cai were executed.

sentences.zh: 謚者，臣議其君，子議其父，而曰「靈」曰「厲」者，不敢以私而亂大猷也，則其餘安可失衷哉！

translations.literal: Posthumous titles are when ministers judge their ruler and sons judge their father—and when one says "Spirit" or "Cruel," one dare not let private feeling disrupt great principles; how then can anything else be allowed to miss the mean!
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous titles are when ministers judge their ruler and sons judge their father—and when one says "Spirit" or "Cruel," one dare not let private feeling disrupt great principles; how then can anything else be allowed to miss the mean!

sentences.zh: 臣竊見節湣太子與李多祚等擁北軍禁旅，上犯宸居，破扉斬關，突禁而入，兵指黃屋，騎騰紫微。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that Prince Jiemin, together with Li Duozuo and others, led the Northern Army's forbidden troops, ascending to violate the imperial residence—smashing gates and breaking barriers, bursting through the forbidden precinct and entering; weapons pointed at the imperial canopy, horsemen surged within the Purple Forbidden Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has observed that Prince Jiemin, together with Li Duozuo and others, led the Northern Army's forbidden troops, ascending to violate the imperial residence—smashing gates and breaking barriers, bursting through the forbidden precinct and entering; weapons pointed at the imperial canopy, horsemen surged within the Purple Forbidden Palace.

sentences.zh: 孝和皇帝移禦玄武門，親降德音，諭以逆順，而太子據鞍自若，督眾不停。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohé moved to the Xuanwu Gate and personally issued an edict of grace, explaining loyalty and rebellion—yet the Heir Apparent sat his saddle at ease and urged his forces on without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaohé moved to the Xuanwu Gate and personally issued an edict of grace, explaining loyalty and rebellion—yet the Heir Apparent sat his saddle at ease and urged his forces on without stopping.

sentences.zh: 俄而其黨悔非，轉逆為順，或回兵討賊，或投狀自拘。

translations.literal: Soon his followers regretted their error and turned rebellion into loyalty—some turned their troops to punish the rebels, others submitted written confessions and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his followers regretted their error and turned rebellion into loyalty—some turned their troops to punish the rebels, others submitted written confessions and restrained themselves.

sentences.zh: 多祚等伏誅，太子方事逃竄。

translations.literal: Li Duozuo and others were executed at the place of punishment, and only then did the Heir Apparent set about fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duozuo and others were executed at the place of punishment, and only then did the Heir Apparent set about fleeing.

sentences.zh: 向使同惡相濟，天道無征，賊徒闕倒戈之人，侍臣虧陛戟之衛，其為禍也，胡可忍言！

translations.literal: If the wicked had aided one another and Heaven had offered no sign, if the rebels had lacked men to turn their blades, if attendants had failed in the guard of halberds at the palace steps—what disaster would have ensued is beyond words!
translations.idiomatic: If the wicked had aided one another and Heaven had offered no sign, if the rebels had lacked men to turn their blades, if attendants had failed in the guard of halberds at the palace steps—what disaster would have ensued is beyond words!

sentences.zh: 於時臣任將作少匠，賜通事舍人內供奉。

translations.literal: At that time your subject held the office of Assistant Master of Palace Construction and was granted status as an Inner Attendant Herald.
translations.idiomatic: At that time your subject held the office of Assistant Master of Palace Construction and was granted status as an Inner Attendant Herald.

sentences.zh: 其明日，孝和皇帝引見供奉官等，雨淚謂曰：「幾不與卿等相見！」

translations.literal: The next day Emperor Xiaohé summoned the attendant officials and, with tears streaming down, said: "I almost failed to see you again!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Emperor Xiaohé summoned the attendant officials and, with tears streaming down, said: "I almost failed to see you again!"

sentences.zh: 其為危懼，不亦甚乎！

translations.literal: How extreme the peril and terror were!
translations.idiomatic: How extreme the peril and terror were!

sentences.zh: 而今聖朝雪罪禮葬，謚為節湣，以臣愚識，竊所惑焉。

translations.literal: Yet now the holy dynasty clears their crimes, buries them with ceremony, and gives the posthumous title Jiemin ("Constant and Lamented")—in your subject's foolish understanding, this is privately perplexing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the holy dynasty clears their crimes, buries them with ceremony, and gives the posthumous title Jiemin ("Constant and Lamented")—in your subject's foolish understanding, this is privately perplexing.

sentences.zh: 夫臣子之禮，嚴敬斯極，故過位必趨，蹙路馬芻有誅。

translations.literal: The rites between minister and ruler reach the utmost in solemn reverence; thus one must quicken one's pace when passing the ruler's place, and even to touch the grass where the ruler's horse passed is punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: The rites between minister and ruler reach the utmost in solemn reverence; thus one must quicken one's pace when passing the ruler's place, and even to touch the grass where the ruler's horse passed is punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 昔漢成之為太子也，行不敢絕馳道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng of Han was Heir Apparent, he dared not travel on the imperial carriage road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng of Han was Heir Apparent, he dared not travel on the imperial carriage road.

sentences.zh: 當周室之衰微也，秦師過周北門，左右免胄而下，王孫滿猶以其不卷甲束兵，譏其無禮，知其必敗。

translations.literal: When the Zhou royal house was in decline, Qin troops passed through the northern gate of Zhou; the attendants doffed their helmets and descended, yet Wangsun Man still reproached them for not rolling up armor and binding their weapons, ridiculed their lack of propriety, and knew they would inevitably be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou royal house was in decline, Qin troops passed through the northern gate of Zhou; the attendants doffed their helmets and descended, yet Wangsun Man still reproached them for not rolling up armor and binding their weapons, ridiculed their lack of propriety, and knew they would inevitably be defeated.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，則太子稱兵宮內，跨馬御前，悖禮已甚矣，況將更甚乎。

translations.literal: From this perspective, for the Heir Apparent to raise troops within the palace and ride his horse before the Emperor—this already transgresses ritual to an extreme; how much more so what actually followed!
translations.idiomatic: From this perspective, for the Heir Apparent to raise troops within the palace and ride his horse before the Emperor—this already transgresses ritual to an extreme; how much more so what actually followed!

sentences.zh: 而可褒謚，此臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: Yet he may be praised with a posthumous title—this your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he may be praised with a posthumous title—this your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 以其斬武三思父子而嘉之乎？

translations.literal: Is it because he beheaded Wu Sansi and his son that he is to be commended?
translations.idiomatic: Is it because he beheaded Wu Sansi and his son that he is to be commended?

sentences.zh: 然弄兵討逆以安君父，則可嘉也，而乃因欲自取之，是競為逆，可褒謚乎？

translations.literal: Yet to wield troops to suppress rebellion and secure lord and father may be praiseworthy; yet because one then wished to seize the throne for oneself, this is competing in rebellion—can he be honored with a posthumous title?
translations.idiomatic: To raise arms against rebels and restore peace to lord and father might be commendable—but to do so because one wished to seize the throne for oneself is to compete in rebellion. Can such a man be honored with a posthumous title?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 將廢韋氏而嘉之乎？

translations.literal: Is it because he deposed the Wei clan that he is to be commended?
translations.idiomatic: Are we to commend him because he deposed the Wei clan?

sentences.zh: 然韋氏逆彰義絕，雖誅之亦可也。

translations.literal: Yet when the Wei clan's rebellion was manifest and righteous ties severed, even putting them to death would have been permissible.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei clan's rebellion was manifest and all righteous bonds severed, even executing them would have been justified.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，韋氏未有逆彰，未有義絕，於太子為母，豈有廢母之理乎！

translations.literal: At that time the Wei clan's rebellion was not yet manifest, righteous ties were not yet severed, and to the Heir Apparent she was his mother—how could there be any justification for deposing one's mother!
translations.idiomatic: At that moment the Wei clan's treason was not yet plain, no righteous bond had been broken, and to the Heir Apparent she was still his mother—what possible justification could there be for deposing one's own mother!

sentences.zh: 且既非中宗之命而廢之，是劫父廢母，亦悖逆也，可褒謚乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, since she was deposed not by Emperor Zhongzong's command but by coercion, this was coercing the father and deposing the mother—also a perverse rebellion. Can he be honored with a posthumous title?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, she was deposed not by Emperor Zhongzong's order but by force—coercing the father and deposing the mother is itself a grave rebellion. Can he be honored with a posthumous title?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 夫君或不君，臣安可不臣？

translations.literal: If the lord fails to act as lord, how can the minister fail to act as minister?
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler fails to rule as he should, how can a minister refuse to serve as a minister must?

sentences.zh: 父或不父，子安可不子？

translations.literal: If the father fails to act as father, how can the son fail to act as son?
translations.idiomatic: If a father fails to father as he should, how can a son refuse to be a son must?

sentences.zh: 借如君父有桀、紂之行，臣子無廢殺之理。

translations.literal: Even suppose the lord and father had the conduct of Jie and Zhou, there is no justification for ministers and sons to depose or kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a ruler and father behaved as Jie and Zhou did, ministers and sons still have no warrant to depose or kill him.

sentences.zh: 況先帝功格宇宙，德被生靈，廟號中宗，謚曰孝和皇帝，而逆命之子，可褒謚乎？

translations.literal: How much more so when the late Emperor's achievements reached heaven and earth, his virtue covered all living beings, his temple title is Zhongzong, and his posthumous title is Emperor Xiaohé—and yet a son who defied his command may be honored with a posthumous title?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when the late Emperor's achievements touched heaven and earth, his virtue embraced all living beings, his temple title is Zhongzong, and his posthumous name is Emperor Xiaohé—and a son who defied his command is to be honored with a posthumous title?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 昔獻公惑驪姬之譖，將殺其太子申生，公子重耳謂之曰：「子盍言子之誌於公乎？」

translations.literal: In antiquity Duke Xian of Jin, deceived by Li Ji's slander, was about to kill his Heir Apparent Shensheng. Prince Chong'er said to him: "Why do you not speak your intentions to the Duke?"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, Duke Xian of Jin, swayed by Li Ji's slanders, was about to execute his Heir Apparent Shensheng. Prince Chong'er said to him, "Why not declare your intentions to the Duke?"

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「不可，君安驪姬，是我傷君之心也。」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent said: "I cannot. If my lord is at ease with Li Ji, for me to speak would wound my lord's heart."
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent replied, "I cannot. If my father is content with Li Ji, then for me to speak would only wound his heart."

sentences.zh: 曰：「然則盍行乎？」

translations.literal: He said: "Then why not flee?"
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er asked, "Then why not flee?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不可，君謂我欲弒君也，天下豈有無父之國哉！

translations.literal: He said: "I cannot. My lord would say I wished to assassinate him—and is there any land under Heaven without a father!
translations.idiomatic: Shensheng answered, "I cannot. My father would believe I meant to kill him—and is there any kingdom under Heaven without a father?

sentences.zh: 吾何行之！」

translations.literal: How could I flee!"
translations.idiomatic: How could I flee!"

sentences.zh: 使人辭於狐突曰：「申生不敢愛其死。

translations.literal: He sent someone to take leave of Hu Tu, saying: "Shensheng does not begrudge his death.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Hu Tu, saying, "Shensheng does not cling to his life.

sentences.zh: 雖然，吾君老矣，子少，國家多難。

translations.literal: Even so, my lord is aged, the heir is young, and the state faces many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my lord is old, the heir is young, and the realm faces many troubles.

sentences.zh: 伯氏茍出而圖吾君，申生受賜而死。」

translations.literal: If you, sir, would go forth and devise plans for my lord, Shensheng will accept the gift of death."
translations.idiomatic: If you, sir, would go forth and counsel my lord, Shensheng will gratefully accept death."

sentences.zh: 再拜稽首，乃自縊。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and touched his head to the ground, then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and touched his forehead to the earth, then hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 其行如是，其謚僅可為恭。

translations.literal: With conduct such as this, his posthumous title could only be Gong ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: Conduct such as this merited a posthumous title no higher than Gong ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 今太子之行反是，可謚為節湣乎？

translations.literal: Today the Heir Apparent's conduct is the opposite of this—can he be given the posthumous title Jiemin?
translations.idiomatic: The present Heir Apparent's conduct was the very reverse—can he be given the posthumous title Jiemin?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝末年，江充與太子有隙，恐帝晏駕後為太子所誅。

translations.literal: In the final years of Emperor Wu of Han, Jiang Chong had a rift with the Heir Apparent and feared that after the Emperor's death he would be executed by the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Wu of Han, Jiang Chong quarreled with the Heir Apparent and feared that once the Emperor died, the Heir Apparent would have him executed.

sentences.zh: 會巫蠱事起，充典理其事。

translations.literal: When the witchcraft scandal arose, Chong was put in charge of investigating it.
translations.idiomatic: When the witchcraft affair broke out, Chong was assigned to investigate it.

sentences.zh: 因此為奸，遂至太子宮掘蠱，得桐木以誣太子。
