translations.literal: Seizing this opportunity for treachery, he went so far as to dig for witchcraft effigies in the Heir Apparent's palace and obtained paulownia wood to frame the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting the occasion for treachery, he dug for witchcraft dolls in the Heir Apparent's palace and planted paulownia wood to incriminate him.

sentences.zh: 時武帝避暑甘泉宮，獨皇后、太子在，太子不能自明，納其少傅石德謀，遂矯節斬充，因敗逃匿。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu was summering at Ganquan Palace; only the Empress and Heir Apparent remained at the capital. Unable to clear himself, the Heir Apparent adopted the counsel of his Junior Tutor Shi De, forged an imperial credential to behead Chong, and upon defeat fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was then at his summer retreat in Ganquan Palace, leaving only the Empress and Heir Apparent in the capital. Unable to prove his innocence, the Heir Apparent followed the advice of his Junior Tutor Shi De, forged an imperial warrant to execute Chong, and after defeat fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 非稱兵詣闕，無逆謀於父，然身死於湖，不葬無謚。

translations.literal: He did not raise troops and march to the palace gate, nor did he harbor rebellious designs against his father—yet he died at Lake, was buried without ceremony, and received no posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: He did not raise an army and march on the palace, nor did he plot rebellion against his father—yet he died at Lake, was buried without honor, and received no posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 至昭帝時，有男子詣北闕自稱衛太子，制使公卿識視，至者莫敢發言。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhao, a man came to the northern gate and proclaimed himself the Wei Heir Apparent. An edict ordered the high ministers to examine and identify him; those who arrived dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhao, a man appeared at the northern gate claiming to be the Wei Heir Apparent. An edict commanded the chief ministers to identify him, but none who came dared speak.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹雋不疑後至，叱從吏收縛之。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Jingzhao, Juan Buyi, arrived later and rebuked his attendant officers to seize and bind him.
translations.idiomatic: Juan Buyi, Commandant of Jingzhao, arrived last and ordered his attendants to seize and bind the man.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「是非未可知，且安之。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Whether this is true or false is not yet known—leave him be for now."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged, "We cannot yet know whether this is true—let us hold him for now."

sentences.zh: 不疑曰：「諸君何患於衛太子。

translations.literal: Buyi said: "What do you gentlemen fear from the Wei Heir Apparent?
translations.idiomatic: Buyi replied, "What do you fear from the Wei Heir Apparent?

sentences.zh: 昔蒯聵出奔，輒拒而不納，《春秋》是之。

translations.literal: In antiquity Kuai Kui fled into exile, and Zhe refused to admit him—the Spring and Autumn Annals approves of this.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Kuai Kui fled into exile and Zhe refused to receive him—the Spring and Autumn Annals commends this.

sentences.zh: 衛太子得罪先帝，亡不即死，今來自詣，此罪人也。」

translations.literal: The Wei Heir Apparent offended the late Emperor, fled without accepting death at once, and now has come of his own accord—this man is a criminal."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Heir Apparent wronged the late Emperor, fled instead of accepting death, and now presents himself of his own accord—he is a criminal."

sentences.zh: 遂送制獄。

translations.literal: He was then sent to the prisons of the imperial secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The man was sent to the imperial prisons.

sentences.zh: 天子聞而嘉之曰：「公卿大臣，當用經術明於大義者。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven heard of this and commended him, saying: "Ministers and great officials ought to be men versed in the classics and clear on great principles."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and praised him, saying, "Ministers and high officials should be men learned in the classics and clear on great principles."

sentences.zh: 及後太子孫立為天子，是曰孝宣皇帝，太子方獲禮葬，而謚曰戾。

translations.literal: Later, when the Heir Apparent's grandson ascended as Son of Heaven—the man known as Emperor Xiao Xuan—the Heir Apparent at last received ceremonial burial, and his posthumous title was Li ("Unruly").
translations.idiomatic: Only later, when the Heir Apparent's grandson ascended the throne as Emperor Xiao Xuan, did the Heir Apparent receive proper burial—and his posthumous title was Li ("Unruly").

sentences.zh: 今節湣太子之行比之，豈可同年而語。

translations.literal: Compared with the conduct of Prince Jiemin today, can the two be spoken of in the same breath?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Prince Jiemin's conduct today, can the two even be mentioned in the same breath?

sentences.zh: 其於陛下，又猶子也，而謚為節湣乎？

translations.literal: With respect to Your Majesty he was moreover like a son—yet he is to be given the posthumous title Jiemin?
translations.idiomatic: To Your Majesty he was, moreover, like a son—and yet he is to receive the posthumous title Jiemin?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 昔項羽之臣丁公，常將危漢高祖，高祖謂之曰：「二賢豈相厄哉！」

translations.literal: In antiquity Ding Gong, a minister of Xiang Yu, once had the power to endanger Emperor Gaozu of Han. Gaozu said to him: "Two worthy men—how could they beset each other!"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Ding Gong, a minister of Xiang Yu, once held Emperor Gaozu of Han at his mercy. Gaozu said to him, "Two worthy men—surely they would not destroy each other!"

sentences.zh: 丁公乃止。

translations.literal: Ding Gong then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gong then stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 及高祖滅項氏，遂戮丁公以徇，曰：「使項王失天下者，丁公也。」

translations.literal: When Gaozu destroyed the house of Xiang, he executed Ding Gong as a warning to all, saying: "The man who made King Xiang lose the empire was Ding Gong."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu overthrew the house of Xiang, he executed Ding Gong before the army, declaring, "The man who made King Xiang lose the empire was Ding Gong."

sentences.zh: 夫戮之，大義至公也，不私德之，所以誡其後之事君者。

translations.literal: To execute him was great principle at its most impartial—he did not indulge private gratitude, thereby to admonish those who would serve lords hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: To kill him was the highest justice, impartial and public—Gaozu would not reward private kindness, so as to warn all who would serve their lords thereafter.

sentences.zh: 今節湣太子之為逆，復非欲保護陛下，其可褒謚乎？

translations.literal: Today Prince Jiemin's rebellion was moreover not to protect Your Majesty—can he be honored with a posthumous title?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiemin's rebellion, moreover, was not undertaken to protect Your Majesty—can he be honored with a posthumous title?

sentences.zh: 此又臣之所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 陛下天縱聖哲，所任賢明，以臣至愚，寧可幹議？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is Heaven-endowed with sagely wisdom and appoints the worthy and enlightened—in my extreme foolishness, how could I intrude with dissent?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Heaven-endowed with sagely wisdom and appoints the worthy and enlightened—for one as foolish as your subject, how dare I presume to remonstrate?

sentences.zh: 然臣又惟堯、舜，聖君也，八凱、五臣，良佐也，猶廣聽芻蕘之言者，蓋為智者千慮，或有一失，愚者千慮，或有一得也。

translations.literal: Yet your subject recalls that Yao and Shun were sage rulers, the Eight Worthies and Five Ministers were fine assistants—yet they still broadly heeded the talk of firewood gatherers, for the wise in a thousand deliberations may have one failure, and the foolish in a thousand deliberations may have one success.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even Yao and Shun, sage rulers though they were, and the Eight Worthies and Five Ministers, fine assistants though they were, still listened widely to the talk of common woodcutters—for in a thousand plans the wise may err once, and in a thousand plans the foolish may succeed once.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「狂夫之言，聖人擇焉。」

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "The words of a madman—the sage selects from them."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Even a madman's words—the sage chooses from among them."

sentences.zh: 臣輒緣斯義，敢以陳聞，願得與議謚者對議於御前。

translations.literal: Your subject, drawing on this principle, ventures to present these views and wishes to debate face to face before Your Majesty with those who deliberated on the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on this principle, your subject ventures to speak and asks to debate before Your Majesty, face to face, with those who set the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 若臣言非也，甘受謗聖政之罪，赴鼎鑊之誅。

translations.literal: If your subject's words are wrong, I will willingly accept the crime of slandering sage governance and submit to execution in the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: If I am wrong, I will gladly accept the charge of slandering sage governance and submit to death in the cauldron.

sentences.zh: 仍請申明義以示天下，使臣輩愚惑者鹹蒙冰釋，則無復異議矣。

translations.literal: I further ask that the right principle be clarified and shown to the empire, so that those of us who are foolishly perplexed may all have our doubts melt like ice, and no further dissent remain.
translations.idiomatic: I further ask that the right principle be made clear to all under Heaven, so that fools like us may have our confusion melt away like ice, and no further dissent remain.

sentences.zh: 若所謚未當，奈何施之聖朝，垂之史冊，使後代逆臣賊子因而引譬，資以為辭，是開悖亂之門，豈示將來之法！

translations.literal: If the posthumous title is improper, how can it be applied in this sage dynasty and handed down in the historical records, so that rebel ministers and wicked sons of later ages may cite it as precedent and use it as pretext—this opens the gate to perverse disorder; how can it serve as law for the future!
translations.idiomatic: If the posthumous title is unfitting, how can it stand in this sage dynasty and pass into the historical record, giving rebel ministers and wicked sons of later ages a precedent and an excuse—opening the gate to rebellion rather than showing the law for generations to come!

sentences.zh: 伏望改定其謚，務合禮經。

translations.literal: I humbly hope the posthumous title will be revised to accord with the rites.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that the posthumous title be revised to accord with the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 其李多祚等罪，請從宥免，不謂為雪，以順天下之心，則盡善盡美矣。

translations.literal: As for the crimes of Li Duozuo and others, I ask that they be pardoned but not called "cleared"—to align with the hearts of all under Heaven would then be perfection itself.
translations.idiomatic: As for Li Duozuo and the others, I ask that their crimes be pardoned but not declared "cleared"—if this accords with the hearts of all under Heaven, all will be perfect indeed.

sentences.zh: 書奏，睿宗引湊謂曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong summoned Cou and said: "It is indeed as you say.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong summoned Cou and said, "What you say is true.

sentences.zh: 事已如此，如何改動？」

translations.literal: Matters have already proceeded thus—how can they be changed?"
translations.idiomatic: Matters have already gone this far—how can they be altered?"

sentences.zh: 湊曰：「太子實行悖逆，不可褒美，請稱其行，改謚以一字。

translations.literal: Cou said: "The Heir Apparent's conduct was truly perverse and rebellious and cannot be praised. I ask that his deeds be named plainly and the posthumous title changed to a single character.
translations.idiomatic: Cou replied, "The Heir Apparent's conduct was truly rebellious and cannot be praised. I ask that his deeds be named plainly and the posthumous title reduced to a single character.

sentences.zh: 多祚等以兵犯君，非曰無罪，只可雲放，不可稱雪。」

translations.literal: Duozuo and others took up arms against the ruler—not to say they are guiltless, but one may only say they were pardoned, not that their offenses were cleared."
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo and the others took up arms against their ruler—not that they were without guilt, but one may say only that they were pardoned, not that their crimes were cleared."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 當時執政以制令已行，難於改易，唯多祚等停贈官而已。

translations.literal: The men then in power, because the edict had already been promulgated, found revision difficult; only the posthumous offices for Duozuo and others were withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Those then in power, finding the edict already issued hard to revise, withheld only the posthumous offices for Duozuo and others.

sentences.zh: 明年春，起金仙、玉真兩觀，用工巨億。

translations.literal: The following spring, the Jin Xian and Yuzhen monasteries were begun, employing labor costing hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, construction began on the Jin Xian and Yuzhen monasteries, at a cost of hundreds of millions in labor.

sentences.zh: 湊進諫曰：「陛下去夏，以妨農停兩觀作，今正農月，翻欲興功。

translations.literal: Cou submitted a remonstrance: "Your Majesty last summer halted construction of the two monasteries to avoid harming agriculture; now in the very month of farming, you wish instead to commence work.
translations.idiomatic: Cou remonstrated: "Your Majesty halted work on the two monasteries last summer to protect the harvest; now, in the very heart of the farming season, you wish to begin again.

sentences.zh: 雖知用公主錢，不出庫物，但土木作起，高價雇人，三輔農人，趨目前之利，舍農受雇，棄本逐末。

translations.literal: Although it is known that the princess's funds are used and nothing comes from the treasury, yet when earth-and-wood construction begins, labor is hired at high wages; farmers of the three metropolitan districts, chasing present profit, abandon farming to accept hire, forsaking the root to pursue the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Though the princess's own funds are used and nothing drawn from the treasury, earth-and-wood construction still hires labor at high wages; farmers of the capital region, tempted by immediate profit, abandon their fields for hire, forsaking the root to chase the branch.

sentences.zh: 臣聞一夫不耕，天下有受其饑者，臣竊恐不可。」

translations.literal: I have heard that if one man does not plough, someone under Heaven goes hungry—I privately fear this cannot be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when one man fails to plough, someone under Heaven goes hungry—I fear this cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 湊又奏曰：「日陽和布氣，萬物生育，土木之間，昆蟲無數。

translations.literal: Cou submitted again: "These days warm yang spreads its breath and the ten thousand things breed and grow; amid earth and timber innumerable insects dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted again: "These days the warm breath of spring spreads abroad and the ten thousand things breed and grow; amid earth and timber countless insects live.

sentences.zh: 此時興造，傷殺甚多，臣亦恐非仁聖本旨。」

translations.literal: Construction at such a time kills many—I also fear this is not the original intent of benevolent sageliness."
translations.idiomatic: Construction at such a season destroys countless lives—I fear this is not the intent of a benevolent and sage ruler."

sentences.zh: 睿宗方納其言，令在外詳議。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong was about to accept his words and ordered detailed deliberation outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong was inclined to accept his advice and ordered further deliberation outside the court.

sentences.zh: 中書令崔湜、侍中岑羲謂湊曰：「公敢言此，大是難事。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui Xian and Palace Attendant Cen Xi said to Cou: "For you, sir, to dare speak thus is a greatly difficult thing."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cui Xian and Palace Attendant Cen Xi told Cou, "For you to speak thus is a bold and difficult thing."

sentences.zh: 湊曰：「叨食厚祿，死且不辭，況在明時，必知不死。」

translations.literal: Cou said: "Receiving a generous stipend, I would not refuse even death—how much more in an enlightened age, when I know I will not die."
translations.idiomatic: Cou replied, "Enjoying a generous stipend, I would not refuse even death—how much more in an enlightened age, when I know I shall not die."

sentences.zh: 尋出為陜州刺史，無幾，轉汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was sent out as prefect of Shaan Prefecture; before long he was transferred to prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed prefect of Shaan; before long he was transferred to prefect of Ru.

sentences.zh: 開元二年夏，敕靖陵建碑，征料夫匠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, summer, an edict ordered a stele erected at Jing Mausoleum and laborers and artisans levied.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan, summer, an edict ordered a stele raised at Jing Mausoleum and laborers and artisans conscripted.

sentences.zh: 湊以自古園陵無建碑之禮，又時正旱儉，不可興功，飛表極諫，工役乃止。

translations.literal: Cou held that from antiquity imperial tombs had no precedent for stele erection, and that at a time of drought and famine construction was impermissible; he submitted an urgent memorial of forceful remonstrance, and the labor ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Cou argued that imperial tombs had never had steles since antiquity, and that in a time of drought and famine construction was impermissible; he submitted an urgent memorial of strong remonstrance, and the work was halted.

sentences.zh: 尋遷岐州剌史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為將作大匠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as Master of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Master of Palace Construction at court.

sentences.zh: 時有敕復孝敬廟為義宗，湊上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time an edict restored the Xiaojing Temple as Yizong; Cou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict restored the Xiaojing Temple under the title Yizong; Cou submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞王者制禮，是曰規模，規模之興，實由師古。

translations.literal: I have heard that the king establishes rites—this is called establishing models; the rise of models in truth derives from taking antiquity as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a king establishes rites to set the pattern of governance, and that such patterns arise from taking antiquity as one's teacher.

sentences.zh: 師古之道，必也正名，名之與實，故當相副。

translations.literal: The way of taking antiquity as teacher requires rectifying names; names and reality must correspond.
translations.idiomatic: The way of learning from antiquity requires rectifying names—name and reality must match.

sentences.zh: 其在宗廟，禮之大者，豈可失哉！

translations.literal: As concerns the ancestral temple, the greatest of rites—how can it be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple lies the greatest of rites—how can it be neglected!

sentences.zh: 禮，祖有功而宗有德，祖宗之廟，百代不毀。

translations.literal: In ritual, those with merit are honored as zu, those with virtue as zong—the temples of zu and zong are not destroyed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual, ancestors of merit are called zu, ancestors of virtue are called zong—and the temples of zu and zong stand for a hundred generations undestroyed.

sentences.zh: 故殷太甲為太宗，太戊曰中宗，武丁曰高宗；

translations.literal: Thus of the Yin, Tai Jia was honored as Taizong, Tai Wu as Zhongzong, and Wu Ding as Gaozong;
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the Yin dynasty Tai Jia was Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, and Wu Ding Gaozong;

sentences.zh: 周宗文王、武王；

translations.literal: of Zhou, King Wen and King Wu were honored as zong;
translations.idiomatic: in Zhou, King Wen and King Wu were honored as zong;

sentences.zh: 漢則文帝為太宗，武帝為世宗。

translations.literal: in Han, Emperor Wen was Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: in Han, Emperor Wen was Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.

sentences.zh: 其後代有稱宗者，皆以方制海內，德澤可宗，列於昭穆，期於不毀。

translations.literal: Thereafter, those given the title zong in successive ages all governed the realm, their virtue and grace worthy of honor, ranked among zhao and mu, expected to endure undestroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, those called zong in every age had governed the realm within the four seas, their virtue and grace worthy of veneration, ranked in the zhao and mu sequence, destined to endure undestroyed.

sentences.zh: 稱宗之義，不亦大乎！

translations.literal: The meaning of the title zong—is it not great indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of the title zong—is it not weighty indeed!

sentences.zh: 伏惟孝敬皇帝位止東宮，未嘗南面，聖道誠冠於儲副，德教不被於寰瀛，立廟稱宗，恐非合禮。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Emperor Xiaojing's rank stopped at the Eastern Palace—he never faced south as ruler; though his sagely virtue indeed surpassed other heirs, his moral teaching did not extend across the seas; to establish a temple and call him zong perhaps does not accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Emperor Xiaojing never ascended beyond the Eastern Palace—he never ruled facing south; though his virtue as heir apparent was supreme, his moral influence did not reach across the seas. To establish a temple and call him zong may not accord with ritual.

sentences.zh: 況別起寢廟，不入昭穆，稽諸祀典，何義稱宗？

translations.literal: Moreover, to build a separate temple outside the zhao-mu sequence—consulting the sacrificial canon, on what grounds call him zong?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a separate temple outside the zhao-mu sequence—consult the sacrificial canon: on what grounds call him zong?

sentences.zh: 而廟號義宗，稱之萬代，以臣庸識，竊謂不可。

translations.literal: Yet the temple title Yizong would be spoken for ten thousand generations—in your subject's shallow understanding, I privately hold this impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the temple title Yizong would be spoken for ten thousand generations—in your subject's humble view, this cannot be right.

sentences.zh: 陛下率循典禮，以辟大猷，有司所議，以致此失，或虧盡善，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty follows the canonical rites to open great designs; what the officials deliberated has led to this error, perhaps falling short of perfection—how can one not regret it!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty follows the canonical rites to establish great governance; what the officials proposed has led to this lapse, falling short of perfection—how can one not regret it!

sentences.zh: 望更詳議，務合於禮。

translations.literal: I hope for further detailed deliberation, so that all accords with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I beg for further deliberation, so that all may accord with ritual.

sentences.zh: 於是敕太常議，遂停義宗之號。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate, and the title Yizong was halted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate, and the title Yizong was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 湊前後上書論時政得失，多見采納。

translations.literal: Cou repeatedly submitted memorials discussing the gains and losses of current policy; many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted memorial after memorial on the strengths and failings of current policy, and many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 再遷河南尹，累封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Intendant of Henan and cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Intendant of Henan and cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以公事左授杭州刺史，轉汾州刺史。

translations.literal: For an official matter he was demoted to prefect of Hang Prefecture, then transferred to prefect of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For an official matter he was demoted to prefect of Hang, then transferred to prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜太原尹兼節度支度營田大使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Intendant of Taiyuan and concurrently Commissioner for Finance, Supply, and Agricultural Colonies of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Intendant of Taiyuan and concurrently Commissioner for Finance, Supply, and Agricultural Colonies.

sentences.zh: 其年卒官，年六十五。

translations.literal: That year he died in office, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in office at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Area Commander of You Prefecture; his posthumous title was Wen ("Refined").
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Area Commander of You; his posthumous title was Wen ("Refined").

sentences.zh: 子見素，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Jiansu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiansu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 湊從子虛心。

translations.literal: Cou's nephew Xuxin.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin was Cou's nephew.

sentences.zh: 虛心父維，少習儒業，博涉文史，舉進士。

translations.literal: Xuxin's father Wei, from youth studied Confucian learning, broadly traversed literature and history, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin's father Wei had studied Confucian learning from youth, gained wide knowledge of literature and history, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 自大理丞累至戶部郎中，善於剖判，時員外郎宋之問工於詩，時人以為戶部有二妙。

translations.literal: From Grand Councilor of the Court of Judicial Review he rose in succession to Department Director in the Ministry of Revenue; he excelled at adjudicating cases. At the time Assistant Director Song Zhiwen was skilled at poetry—the people of the time considered the Ministry of Revenue to have two marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from Grand Councilor in the Court of Judicial Review to Department Director in the Ministry of Revenue, he excelled at adjudication. At the time, Assistant Director Song Zhiwen was renowned for poetry, and the Ministry was said to boast two outstanding talents.

sentences.zh: 終於左庶子。

translations.literal: He ended as Left Assistant Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 虛心舉孝廉，為官嚴整，累至大理丞、侍御史。

translations.literal: Xuxin was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, served as official with strict integrity, rose in succession to Grand Councilor of the Court of Judicial Review and Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin entered service through the Filial and Incorrupt recommendation and governed with strict integrity, rising to Grand Councilor in the Court of Judicial Review and then Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 神龍年，推按大獄，時僕射竇懷貞、侍中劉幽求意欲寬假，虛心堅執法令，有不可奪之誌。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era, investigating and reviewing a major case, at the time Pushe Dou Huaizhen and Palace Attendant Liu Youqiu wished to show leniency; Xuxin firmly upheld the laws and regulations, with a resolve that could not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era, when he investigated a major case, Grand Counselor Dou Huaizhen and Palace Attendant Liu Youqiu wanted leniency, but Xuxin firmly upheld the law with an unshakable resolve.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，西域羌胡背叛，時並擒獲，有敕盡欲誅之。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong period, Qiang and Hu of the Western Regions rebelled; at the time all were captured, and an edict ordered that all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong, Qiang and Hu peoples of the Western Regions rebelled. When they were all captured, an edict was issued ordering their execution.

sentences.zh: 虛心論奏，但罪元首，其所全者千餘人。

translations.literal: Xuxin submitted a memorial arguing that only the leaders should be punished; those he spared numbered more than a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin memorialized the throne, arguing that only the ringleaders should be punished, thus sparing more than a thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 虛心有孝行，及丁父憂，哀毀過禮，須鬢盡白，朝廷深所嗟尚。

translations.literal: Xuxin had filial conduct; when he entered mourning for his father, his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites, his beard and temples turned entirely white, and the court deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin was known for filial devotion. When his father died, his grief exceeded the proper measure of mourning—his beard and temples turned completely white—and the court held him in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 後遷御史中丞、左右丞、兵部侍郎、荊揚潞長史兼采訪使，所在官吏振肅，威令甚舉，中外以為標準。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, Left and Right Assistant Directors, Vice Minister of War, and Chief Administrator of Jing, Yang, and Lu prefectures concurrently Investigation Commissioner; wherever he served, officials were awakened to discipline, his authority and orders were greatly enforced, and both inside and outside the court took him as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Censor-in-Chief, Left and Right Assistant Director, Vice Minister of War, and Chief Administrator of Jing, Yang, and Lu with concurrent duties as Investigation Commissioner. Wherever he served, officials were brought to order and his authority was fully enforced; within and beyond the court, he was regarded as the standard.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部尚書、東京留守，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Revenue and Eastern Capital Regent, died, age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Revenue and Regent of the Eastern Capital before dying at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 季弟虛舟，亦以舉孝廉，自御史累至戶部、司勛、左司郎中，歷荊州長史，洪、魏州刺史兼采訪使，多著能政。

translations.literal: His youngest brother Xuzhou also entered through Filial and Incorrupt recommendation; from Censor he rose in succession to Department Director in the Ministries of Revenue, Personnel Affairs, and the Left Secretariat; served as Chief Administrator of Jingzhou and Prefect of Hong and Wei with concurrent Investigation Commissioner; in many places he showed capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Xuzhou also entered through the Filial and Incorrupt recommendation. Rising from censor to department director in the Ministries of Revenue, Personnel Affairs, and the Left Secretariat, he served as Chief Administrator of Jingzhou and as Prefect of Hong and Wei, concurrently as Investigation Commissioner, and earned a reputation for able governance.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部侍郎，終大理卿。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of Justice, and ended as Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Vice Minister of Justice and ended his career as Chief Justice.

sentences.zh: 家有禮則，父子兄弟更踐郎署，時稱「郎官家」。

translations.literal: The family had rites and regulations; father, sons, and brothers in turn tread the halls of court officials—the age called them the "Family of Court Officials."
translations.idiomatic: The household lived by strict propriety, with fathers, sons, and brothers serving in succession as court officials. They were known in their time as the "Family of Court Officials."

sentences.zh: 韓思復，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Han Sifu was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sifu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖倫，貞觀中為左衛率，賜爵長山縣男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lun, in the Zhenguan period served as General of the Left Guard, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Changshan County.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lun served as General of the Left Guard during Zhenguan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Changshan County.

sentences.zh: 思復少襲祖爵。

translations.literal: Sifu in youth inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu inherited his grandfather's title while still young.

sentences.zh: 初為汴州司戶參軍，為政寬恕，不行杖罰。

translations.literal: At first he was Revenue Section Officer of Bian Prefecture; in governance he was lenient and forgiving, not imposing beating punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Revenue Section Officer in Bian Prefecture, where he governed with leniency and never ordered beatings.

sentences.zh: 在任丁憂，家貧，鬻薪終喪制。

translations.literal: While in office he entered mourning; the family was poor—he sold firewood to complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: While still in office he entered mourning for a parent. The family was poor, so he sold firewood to see out the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 時姚崇為夏官侍郎，知政事，深嘉嘆之，擢授司禮博士。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Chong was Vice Minister of War and attended to government affairs; he deeply praised and sighed over this, and promoted him to be Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong, then Vice Minister of War and a chief policymaker, admired this deeply and had him appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong period, he rose in succession to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong he was promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時左散騎常侍嚴善思坐譙王重福事下制獄，有司言：「善思昔嘗任汝州刺史，素與重福交遊，召至京師，竟不言其謀逆，唯奏雲『東都有兵氣』。

translations.literal: At the time Left Regular Palace Attendant Yan Sansi, implicated in the affair of Prince Qiao Zhongfu, was sent to the specially appointed prison. The responsible officials said: "Sansi formerly served as Prefect of Ru Prefecture, and was accustomed to associate with Zhongfu. When summoned to the capital, he ultimately did not speak of Zhongfu's plot of rebellion, and only submitted saying 'There is a military aura in the Eastern Capital.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time Left Regular Palace Attendant Yan Sansi was implicated in the affair of Prince Qiao Zhongfu and sent to a special prison. The responsible officials reported: "Sansi had once served as Prefect of Ru and was on familiar terms with Zhongfu. Summoned to the capital, he never disclosed Zhongfu's plot, reporting only that 'there is a military aura in the Eastern Capital.'

sentences.zh: 據狀正當匿反，請從絞刑。」

translations.literal: According to the facts, he properly merits concealing rebellion; we request the death penalty by strangulation."
translations.idiomatic: On these facts he should be found guilty of concealing rebellion; we request strangulation."

sentences.zh: 思復駁奏曰：「議獄緩死，列聖明規；

translations.literal: Sifu submitted a refutation memorial, saying: "To debate cases and defer death is the enlightened rule of successive sages;
translations.idiomatic: Sifu submitted a counter-memorial: "Debate in capital cases and defer execution—this is the enlightened rule laid down by successive sage emperors;

sentences.zh: 刑疑從輕，有國常典。

translations.literal: when punishment is doubtful, follow the lighter—this is the standing code of a state.
translations.idiomatic: when the law admits doubt, lean toward leniency—this is a nation's enduring principle.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思往在先朝，屬韋氏擅內，恃寵宮掖，謀危宗社。

translations.literal: Yan Sansi was formerly in the previous court when it fell to the Wei clan to monopolize the inner palace; relying on favor in the palace women quarters, they plotted to endanger the dynastic foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Sansi served in the previous reign when the Wei clan dominated the inner court, wielding favor within the palace and plotting against the dynasty itself.

sentences.zh: 善思此時遂能先覺，因詣相府有所發明，進論聖躬必登宸極。

translations.literal: At this time Sansi was able to perceive it first; therefore he went to the chancellor's office and made certain disclosures, advancing the argument that His Majesty would surely ascend the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi saw the danger early and went to the chancellor's office to reveal what he knew, declaring that His Majesty would surely ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 雖交遊重福，蓋謀陷韋氏。

translations.literal: Although he associated with Zhongfu, it was in order to plot against the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had associated with Zhongfu, he had done so in order to trap the Wei clan.

sentences.zh: 及其謁見，猶不奏聞，將此行藏，即從極法。

translations.literal: When he had an audience, he still did not report it; on this conduct alone, he would receive the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: And for failing to report this when he had an audience, he is to be punished by death—as if that alone were enough to condemn him.

sentences.zh: 且敕追善思，書至便發，向懷逆節，寧即奔命？

translations.literal: Moreover, when the edict summoned Sansi, the letter arrived and he set out at once—if he had harbored treasonous intent, would he have rushed to obey?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the edict summoning Sansi arrived, he set out at once. If he had harbored treasonous intent, would he have obeyed so readily?

sentences.zh: 一面疏網，誠合順生；

translations.literal: On one side to loosen the net—this truly accords with sparing life;
translations.idiomatic: To loosen the net on one side truly accords with mercy and the sparing of life;

sentences.zh: 三驅取禽，來而可宥。

translations.literal: with three drives to take game, those that come may be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: in the three-sided hunt, those who come forward may yet be spared.

sentences.zh: 惟刑是恤，事合昭詳。

translations.literal: To be concerned only with punishment—matters should be made clear and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When punishment is at stake, the matter should be examined in full clarity.

sentences.zh: 請付刑部集群官議定奏裁，以符慎獄。」

translations.literal: I request that this be handed to the Ministry of Justice to gather officials to deliberate and report the decision, to accord with cautious handling of cases."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the case be referred to the Ministry of Justice for deliberation by the full assembly of officials, with their recommendation submitted for imperial decision, in keeping with cautious judgment in capital cases."

sentences.zh: 是時議者多雲善思合從原宥，有司仍執前議請誅之。

translations.literal: At this time many who deliberated said Sansi should receive pardon and mercy, but the responsible officials still held to the previous recommendation requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most who joined the deliberation favored pardoning Sansi, but the responsible officials still pressed their earlier recommendation for execution.

sentences.zh: 思復又駁曰：「臣聞刑人於市，爵人於朝，必僉謀攸同，始行之無惑。

translations.literal: Sifu again submitted a refutation, saying: "Your servant has heard that punishing people in the marketplace and ennobling people at court—these must be of one mind in joint deliberation before they are enacted without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu countered again: "I have heard that executions in the marketplace and ennoblements at court require unanimous deliberation before they are carried out without dispute.

sentences.zh: 謹按諸司所議，嚴善思十才一入，抵罪惟輕。

translations.literal: Respectfully reviewing what the various offices deliberated, on Yan Sansi only one in ten enters guilt; the offense warrants only the lighter penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the deliberations of the various offices on Yan Sansi, only one in ten supports conviction; the offense warrants only the lighter penalty.

sentences.zh: 夫帝閽九重，塗遠千里。

translations.literal: The emperor's gates are ninefold layers, and the road is a thousand li distant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's gates stand nine layers deep, and the road to the throne stretches a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 故借天下之耳以聽，聽無不聰；

translations.literal: Therefore borrow the ears of all under heaven to listen, and in listening nothing is unheard;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor lends his ears to all under heaven, and nothing escapes hearing;

sentences.zh: 借天下之目以視，視無不接。

translations.literal: borrow the eyes of all under heaven to see, and in seeing nothing is unseen.
translations.idiomatic: and lends his eyes to all under heaven, and nothing escapes sight.

sentences.zh: 今群言上聞，采擇宜審，若棄多就少，臣實懼焉。

translations.literal: Now many words have reached the heights; selection should be careful—if one abandons the many for the few, your servant truly fears.
translations.idiomatic: Many opinions have now reached the throne, and the choice among them should be made with care. If the majority view is set aside for the minority, I must confess fear.

sentences.zh: 輿誦一乖，下情不達，雖欲從眾，其可及乎！

translations.literal: If public praise and recitation diverge once, the sentiments below do not reach—though one wishes to follow the multitude, how can that be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: When public opinion and official report diverge, the voices below never reach the throne. Even if one wishes to follow the majority, how can that be done?

sentences.zh: 凡百京司，逢時之泰，列官分職，有賢有親。

translations.literal: All the capital offices, encountering a time of great peace, array their officials and divide duties—there are the worthy and there are the kin.
translations.idiomatic: All the offices of the capital, in this age of peace, divide their duties among officials who are either men of merit or men of kinship.

sentences.zh: 親則列籓諸王，陛下愛子；

translations.literal: The kin are the feudal princes arrayed in order—Your Majesty's beloved sons;
translations.idiomatic: The kin are the princes of the domains—Your Majesty's own beloved sons.

sentences.zh: 賢則胙茅開國，陛下名臣。

translations.literal: the worthy are those enfeoffed with thatched earth and founding states—Your Majesty's eminent ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy are the enfeoffed lords and founding ministers—Your Majesty's most celebrated officials.

sentences.zh: 見無禮於君，寧肯雷同不異？

translations.literal: Seeing lack of propriety toward the ruler—would they willingly agree identically without difference?
translations.idiomatic: When they see impropriety toward the sovereign, would they all simply echo one another without dissent?

sentences.zh: 今措詞多出，法令從輕。」

translations.literal: Now the memorials are many in wording, and the law should follow the lighter."
translations.idiomatic: Memorials on this case are abundant, and the law itself calls for the lighter penalty."

sentences.zh: 上納其奏，竟免善思死，配流靜州。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his memorial, ultimately sparing Sansi from death and assigning him to penal exile in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his memorial and ultimately spared Sansi from death, sentencing him instead to exile in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思復尋轉中書舍人，數上疏陳得失，多見納用。

translations.literal: Sifu soon transferred to Drafting Secretariat Attendant; he repeatedly submitted memorials stating gains and losses, and many were accepted and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was soon made Drafting Secretariat Attendant and repeatedly submitted memorials on matters of policy, many of which the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan, he served as Remonstrance and Consultation Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan period he served as Remonstrance and Consultation Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 時山東蝗蟲大起，姚崇為中書令，奏遣使分往河南、河北諸道殺蝗蟲而埋之。

translations.literal: At the time locusts arose greatly in Shandong; Yao Chong was Director of the Secretariat, and memorialized sending envoys separately to Henan, Hebei, and various circuits to kill locusts and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts swarmed across Shandong, Yao Chong, then Director of the Secretariat, memorialized dispatching envoys throughout Henan, Hebei, and the other circuits to kill the locusts and bury them.

sentences.zh: 思復以為蝗蟲是天災，當修德以禳之，恐非人力所能翦滅。

translations.literal: Sifu considered that locusts are a heaven-sent calamity; one should cultivate virtue to expel them—he feared this was not something human effort could cut down and exterminate.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu held that locust swarms were a heaven-sent calamity, to be averted through cultivation of virtue—not something human effort could simply destroy.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣聞河南、河北蝗蟲，頃日更益繁熾，經歷之處，苗稼都損。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant hears that locusts in Henan and Hebei recently daily become more numerous and fierce; wherever they pass, seedlings and grain are all damaged.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "I have heard that locusts in Henan and Hebei have grown fiercer by the day; wherever they pass, crops are destroyed entirely.

sentences.zh: 今漸翾飛河西，遊食至洛，使命來往，不敢昌言，山東數州，甚為惶懼。

translations.literal: Now they gradually wing west of the river, roaming to feed as far as Luoyang; envoys come and go but dare not speak plainly—several prefectures in Shandong are greatly fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: They are now spreading west of the river toward Luoyang. Official envoys come and go but dare not speak openly, and several Shandong prefectures are gripped by fear.

sentences.zh: 且天災流行，埋瘞難盡。

translations.literal: Moreover, heaven-sent calamities spread widely—burying and interring them is hard to exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when heaven-sent calamity spreads widely, no amount of burying can put an end to it.

sentences.zh: 望陛下悔過責躬，發使宣慰，損不急之務，召至公之人，上下同心，君臣一德，持此誠實，以答休咎。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will repent faults and examine yourself, send envoys to proclaim comfort, reduce non-urgent affairs, summon the most impartial men, above and below of one mind, ruler and ministers of one virtue—holding this sincerity to respond to blessings and calamities.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will repent, examine your own conduct, and send envoys to comfort the people; cut back nonessential tasks, summon the most upright officials, and unite court and country in shared purpose—offering this sincerity in answer to heaven's signs of blessing or disaster.

sentences.zh: 前後驅蝗使等，伏望總停。

translations.literal: The locust-dispatching envoys sent before and after—I humbly hope all will be halted.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that all the locust-suppression envoys already sent be recalled.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：『皇天無親，惟德是輔；

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: 'The August Heaven is not partial—it assists only virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: 'August Heaven is impartial—it assists only those who possess virtue;

sentences.zh: 人心無親，惟惠是懷。』

translations.literal: human hearts are not partial—they embrace only benevolence.'
translations.idiomatic: and the people's hearts are impartial—they embrace only those who show benevolence.'

sentences.zh: 不可不收攬人心也。」

translations.literal: One cannot fail to gather and win human hearts."
translations.idiomatic: One cannot fail to win the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 上深然之，出思復疏以付崇。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved, and issued Sifu's memorial to give to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed strongly and handed Sifu's memorial to Yao Chong.

sentences.zh: 崇乃請遣思復往山東檢蝗蟲所損之處，及還，具以實奏。

translations.literal: Chong then requested sending Sifu to Shandong to inspect the places damaged by locusts; when he returned, he fully reported according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then had Sifu sent to Shandong to inspect locust damage firsthand and, upon his return, report the facts fully to the throne.

sentences.zh: 崇又請令監察御史劉沼重加詳覆，沼希崇旨意，遂箠撻百姓，回改舊狀以奏之。

translations.literal: Chong also requested that Supervising Censor Liu Zhao conduct a further detailed review; Zhao hoping to please Chong's intent, then beat the common people and altered the previous reports to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also sent Supervising Censor Liu Zhao to conduct a follow-up review. Seeking to please Chong, Liu Zhao beat the people and falsified the earlier reports before submitting his findings.

sentences.zh: 由是河南數州，竟不得免。

translations.literal: Because of this, several prefectures in Henan ultimately did not obtain exemption.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, several Henan prefectures were denied tax relief after all.

sentences.zh: 思復遂為崇所擠，出為德州刺史，轉絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Sifu was thus squeezed out by Chong, sent out as Prefect of De Prefecture, transferred to Prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was thus forced out by Chong, first as Prefect of De and then as Prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 入為黃門侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，代裴漼為御史大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, with additional Silver-Gleaming Minister of the Imperial Household, replacing Pei Huan as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, given the additional title Silver-Gleaming Minister of the Imperial Household, and succeeded Pei Huan as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 思復性恬淡，好玄言，安仁體道，非紀綱之任。

translations.literal: Sifu's nature was tranquil and indifferent; he loved abstruse discourse, practicing benevolence and embodying the Way—not the role of enforcing discipline and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was by nature tranquil and fond of philosophical discourse—given to kindness and the cultivation of the Way—not suited to the disciplinary role of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: Before long, he transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died, age over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, at over seventy.

sentences.zh: 子朝宗，天寶初為京兆尹。

translations.literal: His son Chaozong, in early Tianbao served as Intendant of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chaozong served as Intendant of the Capital District in the early Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 曾孫佽，字相之，少有文學，性尚簡淡。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Ci, styled Xiangzhi, in youth had literary learning; his nature prized simplicity and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Ci, courtesy name Xiangzhi, showed literary talent from youth and prized simplicity and restraint in character.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累辟籓方。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to regional posts.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to serve in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 自襄州從事征拜殿中侍御史，遷刑部員外。

translations.literal: From Assistant in Xiang Prefecture he was summoned and appointed Palace Censor in the Hall, transferred to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: From an assistant post in Xiang Prefecture he was summoned to the capital as Palace Censor and later promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 求為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as Prefect of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment as Prefect of Li.

sentences.zh: 歲滿受代，宰相牛僧孺鎮鄂渚，辟為從事，征拜刑部郎中，轉京兆少尹，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he was relieved, Chancellor Niu Sengru garrisoned at Ezhu and recruited him as Assistant; he was summoned and appointed Department Director in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to Vice Intendant of the Capital District, promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, Chancellor Niu Sengru, then stationed at Ezhou, recruited him as an assistant. He was then summoned as Department Director in the Ministry of Justice, became Vice Intendant of the Capital District, and was promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Surveillance Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 桂管二十餘郡，州掾而下至邑長三百員，由吏部而補者什一，他皆廉吏量其才而補之。

translations.literal: Gui Prefecture administered more than twenty commanderies; from Prefecture Assistants down to District Magistrates there were three hundred posts—those filled through the Ministry of Personnel were one in ten; the rest were all filled by measuring the talent of incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gui administered more than twenty prefectures, with three hundred posts from prefectural staff down to district magistrates. Only one in ten was filled through the Ministry of Personnel; the rest were filled by assessing the ability of known incorrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 佽既至桂，吏以常所為官者數百人引謁，一吏執籍而前曰：「具員請補其闕。」

translations.literal: When Ci had arrived at Gui, clerks led several hundred men who regularly served as officials to call upon him; one clerk holding the register came forward and said: "The full complement of posts—we request that vacancies be filled."
translations.idiomatic: When Ci arrived in Gui, clerks presented several hundred men who habitually held local posts. One clerk stepped forward with the register and said: "The roster is full—we request that vacancies be filled."

sentences.zh: 佽戒曰：「在任有政者，不奪所理；

translations.literal: Ci admonished, saying: "Those in office who have governance—do not take away their jurisdictions;
translations.idiomatic: Ci warned them: "Officials who are currently in office and performing competently will not be removed from their jurisdictions;

sentences.zh: 有過者，必繩以法。

translations.literal: those who have faults must be bound by the law.
translations.idiomatic: those who have committed offenses will be dealt with according to law.

sentences.zh: 缺者當俟稽諸故籍，取其可者，然後補之。」

translations.literal: Vacancies should await checking against the old registers, taking those who are acceptable, and then filling them."
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies will be filled only after the old registers are examined and the qualified candidates selected."

sentences.zh: 會春衣使內官至，求賄於郵吏，三豪家因厚其資以求邑宰，佽悉諾之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Spring Clothing envoy arrived from the inner court; he sought bribes from postal clerks, and three powerful families thereupon enriched his funds to seek district magistrates—Ci agreed to all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy for spring clothing arrived, he demanded bribes from the postal officials. Three powerful local families paid him generously to secure district magistracies for their candidates—and Ci appeared to agree to every request.

sentences.zh: 使去，坐以撓法，各笞其背。

translations.literal: When the envoy left, he sat in judgment for obstructing the law, and each was flogged on the back.
translations.idiomatic: After the envoy departed, he punished them for corrupt interference with the law, each receiving a flogging on the back.

sentences.zh: 自是豪猾斂跡，皆得清廉吏以蘇活其人。

translations.literal: From this the powerful and cunning reined in their tracks; all obtained incorrupt officials to revive and sustain the people.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the local power brokers kept their heads down, and incorrupt officials were appointed who brought relief to the people.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔置五管都監，計所費盡一境地征，不足飽其意，佽特用儉約處之，遂為定制，君子以為難。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict established a Five-Circuit Supervisory Commissioner; calculating the expenses would exhaust one entire circuit's levies—not enough to satisfy their desires. Ci especially used frugality and restraint in handling it, and this became a fixed regulation; superior men considered it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict established a Five-Circuit Supervisory Commissioner, whose expenses could consume an entire circuit's tax revenue—yet still fail to satisfy their appetite. Ci managed the post with exceptional frugality, turning his methods into permanent practice; men of judgment regarded this as a notable achievement.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，卒於官，贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng, he died in office; posthumously awarded Vice Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the second year of Kaicheng and was posthumously made Vice Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 張廷珪，河南濟源人，其先自常州徙焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinggui was a man of Jiyuan in Henan; his ancestors migrated there from Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui was a native of Jiyuan in Henan; his family had migrated there from Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廷珪少以文學知名，性慷慨，有誌尚。

translations.literal: Tinggui in youth was known for literary learning; his nature was magnanimous, and he had aspirations and ideals.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui won renown early for his literary talent; he was generous in spirit and held firm ideals.

sentences.zh: 弱冠應制舉。

translations.literal: At weak-crown age he responded to the imperial special examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he took the imperial special examination.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an period, he rose in succession to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he rose to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 則天稅天下僧尼出錢，欲於白司馬阪營建大像。

translations.literal: Empress Wu taxed the monks and nuns throughout the realm to contribute money, intending to build a great image at Baima Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu levied a tax on all monks and nuns in the realm, intending to erect a great Buddha image at Baima Slope.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui memorialized the throne in remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 夫佛者，以覺知為義，因心而成，不可以諸相見也。

translations.literal: As for the Buddha, enlightenment and awareness are his meaning; he is accomplished through the mind—one cannot see him through various forms.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha means awakened awareness: enlightenment arises from the mind itself and cannot be grasped through outward forms.

sentences.zh: 經云：「若以色見我，以音聲求我，是人行邪道，不能見如來。」

translations.literal: The sutra says: "If one sees me through form, seeks me through sound—such a person walks the evil path and cannot see the Thus-Come One."
translations.idiomatic: The sutra says: "He who would see me in form or seek me in sound walks the evil path and cannot perceive the Tathagata."

sentences.zh: 此真如之果不外求也。

translations.literal: This fruit of True Suchness is not to be sought outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: The fruit of true suchness is not to be sought outside oneself.

sentences.zh: 陛下信心歸依，發弘誓願，壯其塔廟，廣其尊容，已遍於天下久矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's faithful heart has taken refuge, issued great vows and aspirations, strengthened tower-temples, broadened revered images—this has already spread throughout the realm for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has long shown sincere faith, taken refuge in the Dharma, made great vows, and endowed temples and icons throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 蓋有住於相而行布施，非最上第一希有之法。

translations.literal: This is dwelling in forms while practicing giving—it is not the most supreme, foremost, rare Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: This is charity that clings to outward form—not the rarest and highest teaching.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: Why do I say this?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 經云：「若人滿三千大千世界七寶以用布施，及恆河沙等身命布施，其福甚多。

translations.literal: The sutra says: "If a person fills the three thousand great thousand-worlds with the seven treasures for giving, and as many body-lives as sands of the Ganges for giving, his merit is very great.
translations.idiomatic: The sutra says: "If one filled three thousand great thousand-worlds with the seven treasures as an offering, or gave one's life as many times as there are sands in the Ganges, the merit would be immense.

sentences.zh: 若人於此經中受持及四句偈等為人演說，其福勝彼。」

translations.literal: If a person in this sutra upholds and receives, and even a four-line verse and the like expounds for others, his merit surpasses that."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if one upholds even a four-line verse from this sutra and expounds it to others, the merit surpasses all of that."

sentences.zh: 如佛所言，則陛下傾四海之財，殫萬人之力，窮山之木以為塔，極冶之金以為像，雖勞則甚矣，費則多矣，而所獲福不愈於一禪房之匹夫。

translations.literal: As the Buddha said, then Your Majesty would expend the wealth of the four seas, exhaust the strength of ten thousand men, exhaust mountain timber to make pagodas, and use all smelted gold to make images—though the labor is very great and the expense very much, yet the merit obtained is not better than that of a single common man in a meditation hall.
translations.idiomatic: As the scripture teaches, if Your Majesty pour out the wealth of the empire, exhaust the labor of countless men, strip the mountains for timber to build pagodas, and pour all refined gold into images—even at such enormous cost and toil—the merit gained would not exceed that of one solitary layman in a chan cell.

sentences.zh: 菩薩作福德，不應貪著，蓋有為之法不足高也。

translations.literal: Bodhisattvas performing meritorious deeds should not be greedy and attached; indeed, conditioned dharmas are not sufficient to be esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When bodhisattvas cultivate merit, they must not grow attached to it; the methods of conditioned action are unworthy of exaltation.

sentences.zh: 況此營建，事殷木土，或開發盤礴，峻築基階，或塞穴洞，通轉采斫，輾壓蟲蟻，動盈巨億。

translations.literal: Moreover this construction, the affair is abundant in wood and earth; sometimes opening and developing vast terrain, steeply building foundations and steps, sometimes blocking caves and holes, turning to cut and hew timber, crushing insects and ants—movement fills tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, these building projects entail immense earthworks and timber: hillsides are quarried and foundations raised on steep terraces; caves are sealed off while timber is cut and hauled through every passage—and in the crush, countless insects and ants are ground underfoot, in numbers beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 豈佛標坐夏之義，湣蠢動而不忍害其生哉！

translations.literal: How could this be the Buddha's marking of the meaning of summer retreat, pitying moving things and unable to bear harming their lives!
translations.idiomatic: Can this be what the Buddha meant by the summer retreat—compassion for every living creature and unwillingness to destroy a single life?

sentences.zh: 又役鬼不可，唯人是營，通計工匠，率多貧窶，朝驅暮役，勞筋苦骨，簞食瓢飲，晨炊星飯，饑渴所致，疾疹交集。

translations.literal: Again, employing ghosts is impossible; only humans are the workers. Calculating the craftsmen in total, most are poor and destitute, driven in the morning and laboring in the evening, toiling sinew and bittering bone, eating from a bamboo basket and drinking from a gourd, cooking at dawn and eating by starlight, hunger and thirst bringing disease and rash together in intersection.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits cannot be pressed into service—only human beings bear the work. The craftsmen are overwhelmingly poor and wretched, driven from dawn to dusk until sinews ache and bones are worn out. They subsist on meager fare, cook before daylight and eat by starlight, and from hunger and thirst sickness and fever multiply.

sentences.zh: 豈佛標徒行之義，湣畜獸而不忍殘其力哉！

translations.literal: How could this be the Buddha's marking of the meaning of traveling on foot, pitying beasts of burden and unable to bear wasting their strength!
translations.idiomatic: Is this what the Buddha meant by traveling on foot—compassion for beasts of burden and unwillingness to waste their strength?

sentences.zh: 又營築之資，僧尼是稅，雖乞丐所致，而貧闕猶多。

translations.literal: Again, funds for construction are levied on monks and nuns; though solicited by begging, the poor and lacking are still many.
translations.idiomatic: Construction funds are extracted even from monks and nuns, who may beg for alms—yet many remain in want.

sentences.zh: 州縣征輸，星火逼迫，或謀計靡所，或鬻賣以充，怨聲載路，和氣未洽。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties collect and transport tribute, urgent as sparks and meteors pressing; some have nowhere to scheme, some sell property to fulfill it, sounds of resentment fill the roads, harmonious qi is not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties press for levy with urgent haste; families find nowhere to turn, and some sell their possessions to meet the demand. Resentment fills the roads, and concord has not returned.

sentences.zh: 豈佛標隨喜之義，湣愚蒙而不忍奪其產哉！

translations.literal: How could this be the Buddha's marking of the meaning of rejoicing in others' merit, pitying the foolish and ignorant and unable to bear seizing their property!
translations.idiomatic: Can this accord with the Buddha's teaching of rejoicing in others' merit—with pity for the simple and no wish to strip them of their livelihood?

sentences.zh: 且邊朔未寧，軍裝日給，天下虛竭，海內勞弊。

translations.literal: Moreover the northern frontier is not yet settled, military supplies daily provided, the realm is emptied and exhausted, within the seas labor and weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the northern marches remain unsettled, military supplies must be furnished daily, the realm is drained empty, and the whole empire labors under exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下慎之重之，思菩薩之行為利益一切眾生，應如是布施，則其福德若南西北方四維上下虛空不可思量。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty should be careful and weigh this heavily, thinking on the bodhisattva's conduct as benefiting all sentient beings—giving should accord with this; then the meritorious virtue would be like south, north, west, east, the four corners, above and below, empty space—immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: I implore Your Majesty to reflect carefully: consider how the bodhisattva's path benefits all living beings. Charity in that spirit would yield merit as vast as the heavens in every direction—as boundless as space itself.

sentences.zh: 夫何必勤於住相，雕蒼生之業，崇不急之務乎！

translations.literal: Why must one be diligent in dwelling in marks, carving the livelihood of the dark masses, elevating non-urgent affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Why then insist on clinging to outward forms, carving up the people's substance to glorify matters that can wait?

sentences.zh: 臣以時政論之，則宜先邊境，蓄府庫，養人力；

translations.literal: Your servant, discussing current administration, says one should first secure the borders, store the treasuries, nurture human strength;
translations.idiomatic: Speaking as a matter of state, the priority should be securing the frontier, filling the treasury, and conserving manpower;

sentences.zh: 臣以釋教論之，則宜救苦厄，滅諸相，崇無為。

translations.literal: Your servant, discussing the Buddhist teaching, says one should save from suffering and calamity, extinguish all marks, and esteem non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking as a matter of Buddhist doctrine, the priority should be relieving suffering, transcending all outward distinctions, and upholding the ideal of non-action.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下察臣之愚，行佛之意，務以理為上，不以人廢言，幸甚幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to examine your servant's foolishness, practice the Buddha's intent, striving to take reason as supreme, not dismissing words on account of the person—most fortunate, most fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will consider my humble counsel, heed the Buddha's true meaning, value principle above all, and judge the argument rather than the arguer. This would be a great fortune indeed.

sentences.zh: 則天從其言，即停所作，仍於長生殿召見，深賞慰之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu followed his words, immediately stopping what was being done, and moreover summoned him at Changsheng Hall, deeply commending and comforting him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian took his counsel and immediately halted the construction. She then received him at Changsheng Hall and praised and consoled him warmly.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，為中書舍人，再轉洪州都督，仍為江南西道按察使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jinglong era, he served as Secretariat Drafter; twice transferred to Governor of Hong Prefecture, and additionally served as Jiangnan West Circuit Investigator.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Jinglong reign he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, then twice promoted to military governor of Hong Prefecture, concurrently serving as regional inspector of Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 開元初，入為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, he entered [the capital] as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaiyuan reign he was recalled to the capital as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時久旱，關中饑儉，下制求直諫昌言、弘益政理者。

translations.literal: At that time there was long drought; Guanzhong suffered famine and scarcity. An edict was issued seeking straight remonstrance, forthright speech, and those who would expand and benefit governance.
translations.idiomatic: A prolonged drought had gripped the land; the Guanzhong region faced famine. The throne issued an edict calling for candid remonstrance and counsel to improve governance.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上疏曰：

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古有多難興王、殷憂啟聖者，皆以事危則誌銳，情迫則思深，故能自下登高，轉禍為福者也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in antiquity, kings who rose amid many difficulties and sages who were awakened by deep sorrow—all took the approach that when affairs are perilous the will is sharp, when circumstances press the thought is deep, and thus able to rise from low to high, turn calamity into fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that in antiquity, rulers who triumphed through adversity and sages forged in crisis all shared one truth: when danger sharpens the will and necessity deepens reflection, one can rise from the lowest station and turn misfortune into blessing.

sentences.zh: 伏見景龍之末，中宗遇禍，先天之際，兇黨構謀，社稷有危於綴旒，國朝將均於絕綖。

translations.literal: I humbly observe at the end of Jinglong, Zhongzong met calamity; at the time of Xiantian, wicked factions plotted treachery—the altars of soil and grain had danger like a dangling tassel, the dynastic court was about to share the fate of a broken cord.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that at the end of the Jinglong era Emperor Zhongzong met a violent end; during the Xiantian coup, treacherous factions plotted—the empire hung by a thread, and the dynasty itself stood on the brink of collapse.

sentences.zh: 陛下神武超代，精誠動天，再掃氛沴，六合清朗。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's divine martial prowess surpassed the age, sincere devotion moved heaven, again sweeping away baleful vapors—the six directions clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's martial brilliance surpasses any age, and your sincerity moved heaven itself. You swept away the miasma of chaos, and the realm is once again bright and clear.

sentences.zh: 而後上順皇旨，俯念黔黎，高運璿衡，光膺寶箓。

translations.literal: Afterwards ascending in accord with Heaven's mandate, bowing in mind to the black-haired masses, loftily turning the jade armillary, brightly receiving the sacred scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter you ascended in harmony with Heaven's intent, turned your mind to the common people, governed with the precision of the celestial sphere, and received the sacred mandate of rule.

sentences.zh: 日月所燭之地，書軌未通之鄉，無不霑濡渥恩，被服淳化。

translations.literal: All places illuminated by sun and moon, all villages where written records and cart tracks had not reached—none failed to receive abundant grace, clothed in pure transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Every land the sun and moon shine upon, every region where civilization had not yet reached—all have bathed in your generous grace and been wrapped in your benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 十堯、九舜，未足稱也。

translations.literal: Even ten Yaos and nine Shuns would not suffice for praise.
translations.idiomatic: Not even ten emperors like Yao and nine like Shun together would suffice for praise.

sentences.zh: 明明上帝，照臨下土，宜錫介祉，以答鴻休。

translations.literal: The bright bright Lord on High, shining down upon the lower earth, should bestow great blessing to answer vast felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The clear-eyed Lord on High looks down upon the earth; surely He will grant great blessings to answer so magnificent a reign.

sentences.zh: 然屬頃歲已來，陰陽愆候，九谷失稔，萬姓阻饑，關輔之間，更為尤劇。

translations.literal: Yet recently in these years, yin and yang have missed their seasons, the nine grains have failed ripening, the myriad people obstructed by famine—in the Guanfu region it is especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years the seasons have fallen out of harmony, the harvests have failed, and famine has strangled the people—nowhere more severely than in the Guanzhong heartland.

sentences.zh: 至有樵蘇莫爨，糧籺靡資，不復聊生，方憂轉死。

translations.literal: There are even those with firewood and kindling who cannot cook, grain provisions with no resources, no longer able to sustain life, just now fearful of dying in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Some have wood for fuel yet cannot cook a meal; others lack even coarse grain and cannot go on living, fearing only that death will come next.

sentences.zh: 偶會昌運，遘茲難否者，臣竊思之，皇天之意，將恐陛下春秋鼎盛，神聖在躬，不崇朝而建大功，自籓邸而陟元後，或簡下濟之道，獨滿雄圖之誌，輕虞舜而不法，思漢武以自高。

translations.literal: Those who by chance meet a prosperous age and encounter this difficulty and denial—or so your servant privately considers—Heaven's intent is perhaps that Your Majesty, in the prime of youth, with the sacred in your person, having established great merit not in a morning, ascending from the princely residence to the primal sovereign, may abbreviate the way of succoring the lower realm, alone filling the ambitious will, lightly taking Yao and Shun as models without following them, thinking to match Emperor Wu in self-exaltation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who have met this prosperous age only to suffer such affliction—I believe Heaven's intent may be to warn Your Majesty. In the prime of life, with sacred talent in your person, you rose from princely quarters to the throne in a single stroke. Perhaps Heaven wishes to test whether you will neglect the duty of nourishing the people, indulge ambition alone, look down on the models of Yao and Shun, and emulate the hubris of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 是故昭見咎征，載加善誘，將欲大君日慎一日，雖休勿休，永保太和，以固邦本也。

translations.literal: Therefore manifestations appear and portents of blame are displayed, repeatedly adding good guidance, intending that the great lord daily be cautious day by day, though at rest not resting, forever preserving great harmony to solidify the state's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Heaven has sent visible signs of warning and repeated admonishments, wishing the sovereign to grow more vigilant day by day—to find no rest even in prosperity, to preserve great harmony, and to secure the foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 斯皇天於陛下睠顧深矣，陛下焉可不奉若休旨而寅畏哉！

translations.literal: This is Imperial Heaven's deep care and regard for Your Majesty—how can Your Majesty not reverently follow the auspicious intent with respectful awe!
translations.idiomatic: How deeply Heaven has watched over Your Majesty! How could you fail to heed these warnings with reverence and awe?

sentences.zh: 臣愚誠願陛下約心削誌，澄思勵精，考羲、農之書，敦素樸之道。

translations.literal: Your servant in foolish sincerity wishes Your Majesty to restrain the heart and reduce ambition, clarify thought and encourage refinement, examine the books of Fu Xi and Shen Nong, and honor the way of plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly urge Your Majesty to restrain your passions and curb your ambitions, clarify your mind and steel your resolve, study the classics of Fu Xi and Shen Nong, and embrace the path of plain simplicity.

sentences.zh: 登庸端士，放黜佞人，屏退後宮，減徹外廄，場無蹴⻊匊之玩，野絕從禽之賞。

translations.literal: Elevate upright scholars, dismiss and banish flatterers, retire the inner palaces, reduce and eliminate outer stables, the grounds without kickball playthings, the wilds ended of hunting-for-bird rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Promote upright men of talent, dismiss sycophants, keep the harem at a distance, cut back the imperial stables, ban cuju games from the palace grounds, and forsake the pleasure of hunting in the fields.

sentences.zh: 休石田之遠境，罷金甲之懸軍，矜恤煢嫠，蠲薄徭賦。

translations.literal: Rest from stony fields in distant borders, halt gold-armored suspended armies, pity and care for the lonely and widowed, remit and reduce corvée levies and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Leave fallow the barren fields on distant borders, withdraw the armies stationed in far garrisons, show compassion to widows and orphans, and lighten corvée and taxation.

sentences.zh: 去奇伎淫巧，捐和璧隋珠，不見可欲，使心不亂。

translations.literal: Remove strange skills and wanton craft, discard the He bi and Sui pearl, not seeing desirable things, making the heart not chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Discard ingenious frivolities and luxurious baubles, renounce treasures such as the jade disk of He and the pearls of Sui—give your heart no object of desire, and it will not be distracted.

sentences.zh: 自然波清四海，塵銷九域，農夫樂其業，餘糧棲於畝。

translations.literal: Naturally waves will clear the four seas, dust will vanish in the nine regions, farmers will rejoice in their occupations, surplus grain will rest in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Then naturally the four seas will be calm, the realm will be cleared of turmoil, farmers will delight in their work, and surplus grain will fill the furrows.

sentences.zh: 則和氣上通於天，雖五星連珠，兩曜合璧，未足多也；

translations.literal: Then harmonious qi will ascend and connect with Heaven—even the five stars joining in pearls, the two luminaries joining disks, would not be worth much;
translations.idiomatic: Then the harmonious breath will rise to Heaven—and even such marvels as five planets in alignment or the sun and moon conjoined would not be worth mentioning;

sentences.zh: 珍祥下降於地，雖鳳皇巢閣，麒麟在郊，未足奇也。

translations.literal: Precious auspice will descend to earth—even the phoenix nesting on a pavilion, the qilin in the suburbs, would not be worth marvel.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious omens may descend to earth—even a phoenix nesting in the palace or a qilin appearing in the suburbs would scarcely be remarkable.

sentences.zh: 或謂天之炯戒不足畏者，則將上帝憑怒，風雨迷錯，荒饉日甚，無以濟下矣。

translations.literal: If some say Heaven's bright warning is not sufficient to be feared, then Lord on High will lean on anger, wind and rain will err and confuse, wild famine daily worsen—there will be no means to succor the lower realm.
translations.idiomatic: Should anyone deem Heaven's clear warning unworthy of fear, the Lord on High will be roused to anger—wind and rain will fall into disorder, famine will worsen daily, and there will be no way to save the people below.

sentences.zh: 或謂人之窮乏不足恤者，則將齊甿沮誌，億兆攜離，愁苦勢極，無以奉上矣。

translations.literal: If some say people's destitution and lack are not sufficient to be pitied, then uniformly the farmers will be discouraged in will, hundreds of millions will scatter in separation, grief and bitterness will reach extreme force—there will be no means to serve the above.
translations.idiomatic: Should anyone deem the people's impoverishment unworthy of pity, the farmers will lose all heart, the multitudes will scatter in rebellion, misery will reach its limit—and there will be no one left to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋安危所系，禍福之源，奈何朝廷曾不是察！

translations.literal: This indeed is what safety and danger hinge upon, the source of calamity and fortune—how is it that the court never examines this!
translations.idiomatic: These are the very matters on which safety and ruin depend, the wellspring of blessing and disaster—yet how has the court failed to perceive them!

sentences.zh: 況今陛下受命伊始，敷政惟新，卿士百僚，華夷萬族，莫不清耳以聽，刮目而視，延頸企踵，冀有所聞見，颙颙如也。

translations.literal: Moreover now Your Majesty at the beginning of receiving the mandate, spreading governance only newly—the ministers and hundred officials, Chinese and barbarian myriad tribes—none failed to clear the ears to listen, rub the eyes to look, stretch the neck and stand on tiptoe, hoping to hear and see something, eager and looking upward.
