translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty has only just received the mandate and inaugurated a new reign; ministers and officials, Chinese and barbarian peoples alike—all listen with rapt attention, watch with renewed eyes, and crane their necks in anticipation, hoping to witness something worthy. The whole realm looks to you with expectation.

sentences.zh: 何可怠棄典則，坐辜其望哉！

translations.literal: How can one be idle and abandon canonical standards, sitting and failing their hopes!
translations.idiomatic: How can you idle away established norms and betray these hopes!

sentences.zh: 再遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史蔣挺以監決杖刑稍輕，敕朝堂杖之，廷珪奏曰：「御史憲司，清望耳目之官，有犯當殺即殺，當流即流，不可決杖。

translations.literal: At that time Investigating Censor Jiang Ting, because the supervised execution of the cudgel punishment was slightly light, was ordered beaten at the court hall. Tinggui memorialized saying: "The censor is of the law office, a clean and eminent ear-and-eye official—if there is offense, when execution is due execute, when exile is due exile; the cudgel decision cannot be applied.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Jiang Ting was judged to have supervised a flogging too leniently, the throne ordered him beaten in the court hall. Tinggui submitted a memorial: "Censors serve as the eyes and ears of justice—a position of honorable repute. If guilty, let him be executed or exiled—but not flogged.

sentences.zh: 士可殺，不可辱也。」

translations.literal: A scholar may be killed but cannot be humiliated."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman may be killed, but he cannot be humiliated."

sentences.zh: 時制命已行，然議者以廷珪之言為是。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial order had already been carried out, yet those discussing considered Tinggui's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Though the order had already been carried out, public opinion sided with Tinggui.

sentences.zh: 俄坐泄禁中語，出為沔州刺史，又歷蘇、宋、魏三州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after, convicted of leaking palace secrets, sent out as Prefect of Mian, then served successively as Prefect of Su, Song, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was convicted of leaking palace secrets and demoted to prefect of Mian; he later served in succession as prefect of Su, Song, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 入為少府監，加金紫光祿大夫，封范陽男。

translations.literal: Entered the capital as Director of the Palace Workshops, with additional title Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Director of the Palace Workshops, granted the additional title Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, and enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 四遷太子詹事，以老疾致仕。

translations.literal: Promoted four times to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; due to old age and illness, retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After four further promotions he became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; he then retired on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，年七十余，贈工部尚書，謚曰貞穆。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, age over seventy; posthumously granted Minister of Works; posthumous title Zhenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year of the reign, aged over seventy; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Zhenmu, "Upright and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 廷珪素與陳州刺史李邕親善，屢上表薦之，邕所撰碑碣之文，必請廷珪八分書之。

translations.literal: Tinggui had long been friendly with Li Yong, Prefect of Chen; repeatedly memorialized recommending him; for inscriptions on steles Li Yong composed, he always requested Tinggui's clerical-script calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui had long been close to Li Yong, prefect of Chen, and repeatedly recommended him in memorials. For every stele inscription Li Yong composed, he would ask Tinggui to write it in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 廷珪既善楷隸，甚為時人所重。

translations.literal: Tinggui was skilled at regular and clerical script, greatly valued by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui excelled at regular and clerical script and was held in high esteem by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 王求禮，許州長社人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiuli, native of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli was a native of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則天朝為左拾遺，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: During Wu Zetian's reign he served as Left Reminder, transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he served as Left Reminder and was later promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 性忠謇敢言，每上封彈事，無所畏避。

translations.literal: His nature was loyal and forthright, daring in speech; every sealed memorial impeaching affairs, nothing feared or avoided.
translations.idiomatic: He was loyal and outspoken by nature; in every sealed memorial of impeachment he held nothing back and feared no one.

sentences.zh: 時契丹李盡忠反叛，其將孫萬榮寇陷河北數州，河內王武懿宗擁兵討之，畏懦不敢進。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled; his general Sun Wanrong invaded and captured several prefectures in Hebei; Wang Wuzong of Henei led troops to suppress them, fearful and cowardly, not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan leader Li Jinzhong rebelled, his general Sun Wanrong overran several prefectures in Hebei. Wang Wuzong of Henei took command of the punitive force but, timid and irresolute, dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 既而賊大掠而去，懿宗條奏滄、瀛百姓為賊詿誤者數百家，請誅之。

translations.literal: Afterwards the bandits plundered greatly and departed; Wuzong itemized and memorialized several hundred households among Cang and Ying common people who were deceived and misled by bandits, requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels had looted the region and withdrawn, Wuzong drew up a list of several hundred households in Cang and Ying whom he claimed had been misled by the enemy, and requested that they be executed.

sentences.zh: 求禮執而劾之曰：「此詿誤之人，比無良吏教習，城池又不完固，為賊驅逼，茍徇圖全，豈素有背叛之心哉！

translations.literal: Qiuli seized and impeached him, saying: "These deceived and misled people, compared with having no good officials to teach them, city walls also not complete and solid, driven by bandits and pressed, temporarily following to preserve wholeness—how could they have had rebellious hearts from the start!
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli detained him and impeached him, saying: "These people were misled. They had no capable officials to guide them, their walls were not strong, and when the enemy drove them on they submitted only to save themselves—how could they have harbored treason from the start?

sentences.zh: 懿宗擁強兵數十萬，聞賊將至，走保城邑，罪當誅戮。

translations.literal: Wuzong held strong troops numbering hundreds of thousands; hearing bandits were about to arrive, he ran to protect city and towns—crime should be execution.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong commanded an army of hundreds of thousands, yet when he heard the enemy was coming he fled behind city walls—a crime deserving death.

sentences.zh: 今乃移禍於詿誤之人，豈是為臣之道？

translations.literal: Now shifting calamity onto deceived and misled people—is this the way of a minister?
translations.idiomatic: Now you would shift the blame onto those who were misled—is this the conduct of a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 請斬懿宗以謝河北百姓。」

translations.literal: I request executing Wuzong to apologize to the common people of Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Wuzong be executed to answer to the people of Hebei."

sentences.zh: 懿宗大懼，則天竟降制赦之。

translations.literal: Wuzong greatly feared; Wu Zetian ultimately lowered an edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was terrified, and Wu Zetian ultimately issued an edict pardoning the accused.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷幽州，饋輓不給，左相豆盧欽望請輟京官兩月俸料以助軍，求禮謂欽望曰：「公祿厚俸優，輟之可也。

translations.literal: The Khitan captured Youzhou; supply transport was not provided. Left Chancellor Dou Lu Qinwang requested halting capital officials' two months' salary to aid the army. Qiuli said to Qinwang: "Your public salary is thick and stipend generous—halting it is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan captured Youzhou and supply lines failed, Left Chancellor Dou Lu Qinwang proposed suspending two months' salary for capital officials to support the army. Qiuli told him: "Your own salary is generous—yours could be spared.

sentences.zh: 國家富有四海，足以儲軍國之用，何藉貧官薄俸。

translations.literal: The state is rich in the four seas, sufficient to store military and state use—why rely on poor officials' thin salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is wealthy enough to meet every military and state need—why must you lean on the meager pay of impoverished officials?

sentences.zh: 公此舉豈宰相法邪？」

translations.literal: Is this action worthy of a chancellor's standard?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this how a chancellor is supposed to act?"

sentences.zh: 欽望作色拒之，乃奏曰：「秦、漢皆有稅算以贍軍，求禮不識大體，妄有訟辭。」

translations.literal: Qinwang changed color and refused; then memorialized saying: "Qin and Han both had tax arithmetic to support the army; Qiuli does not know the great principle, recklessly having litigation words."
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang flushed with anger and rebuffed him, then memorialized: "Both Qin and Han levied special taxes to support their armies. Qiuli fails to grasp the larger picture and recklessly picks quarrels."

sentences.zh: 求禮對曰：「秦皇、漢武稅天下，虛中以事邊，奈何使聖朝則效？

translations.literal: Qiuli replied: "Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu taxed the realm, emptied the center to serve the border—how can you make the holy court follow their example?
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli replied: "Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu taxed the empire hollow to fund their frontier wars—would you have our sage dynasty imitate them?

sentences.zh: 不知欽望此言是大體耶！」

translations.literal: I do not know whether Qinwang's words are the great principle!"
translations.idiomatic: I wonder whether Chancellor Qinwang's proposal is the larger picture after all!"

sentences.zh: 事遂不行。

translations.literal: The matter then did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時三月雪，鳳閣侍郎蘇味道等以為瑞，草表將賀，求禮止之曰：「宰相調燮陰陽，而致雪降暮春，災也，安得為瑞？

translations.literal: At that time in the third month it snowed; Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Su Weidao and others considered it auspicious, drafted a memorial to congratulate. Qiuli stopped them, saying: "The chancellor harmonizes yin and yang, yet snow falls in late spring—calamity; how can it be auspicious?
translations.idiomatic: When snow fell in the third month, Vice Minister Su Weidao and others took it for a good omen and drafted a congratulatory memorial. Qiuli stopped them: "It is the chancellor's duty to harmonize yin and yang—yet snow falls in late spring. That is a calamity, not an omen.

sentences.zh: 如三月雪為瑞雪，則臘月雷亦瑞雷也。」

translations.literal: If snow in the third month is auspicious snow, then thunder in the twelfth month is also auspicious thunder."
translations.idiomatic: If snow in the third month counts as an auspicious snow, then thunder in the twelfth month must count as an auspicious thunder."

sentences.zh: 舉朝嗤笑，以為口實。

translations.literal: The whole court sneered, taking it as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court laughed at the affair, and it became a standing joke.

sentences.zh: 求禮竟以剛正，名位不達而卒。

translations.literal: Qiuli ultimately due to stern uprightness, name and rank did not advance, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli remained so upright and unyielding that he never rose high in rank and died without advancement.

sentences.zh: 辛替否，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Xin Tifou, native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifou was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 景龍年為左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he served as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong reign he served as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時中宗置公主府官屬，安樂公主府所補尤多猥濫。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongzong established princess household staff; Princess Anle's appointments were especially numerous and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Zhongzong established official staffs for the princesses, and the appointments to Princess Anle's household were especially numerous and indiscriminate.

sentences.zh: 又駙馬武崇訓死後，棄舊宅別造一宅，侈麗過甚。

translations.literal: Again, after Consort Wu Chongxun died, they abandoned the old residence and separately built a new mansion, extravagance passing measure.
translations.idiomatic: After the death of her consort Wu Chongxun, she abandoned the old residence and built a new mansion, with extravagance beyond all measure.

sentences.zh: 時又盛興佛寺，百姓勞弊，帑藏為之空竭。

translations.literal: At that time Buddhist temples also flourished greatly; common people labored in weariness, the treasury for it empty and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist construction was also flourishing at the time, exhausting the people and draining the treasury empty.

sentences.zh: 替否上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Tifou submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之建官，員不必備，九卿以下，皆有其位而闕其選。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in antiquity establishing offices, posts were not necessarily filled; below the Nine Ministers, all had their positions but lacked appointees.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in antiquity, when offices were established, not every post was filled; even below the rank of Nine Ministers, many positions existed but appointees were left vacant.

sentences.zh: 賞一人謀乎三事，職一人訪乎群司，負寵者畏權勢之在躬，知榮者避權門而不入。

translations.literal: Rewarding one person, deliberating on the three affairs; assigning one person, inquiring among all departments—those bearing favor feared power and position in their person; those knowing glory avoided power gates and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When one man was rewarded, the three chief ministers would deliberate; when one man was appointed, every department would be consulted. Those who enjoyed favor feared the burden of power; men of honor shunned the gates of influence and would not enter them.

sentences.zh: 故稱賞不僭，官不濫，士皆完行，家有廉節，朝廷有餘俸，百姓有餘食。

translations.literal: Therefore praise was not excessive, offices not excessive; scholars all had complete conduct, families had integrity; the court had surplus salary, common people had surplus food.
translations.idiomatic: Thus rewards were not lavish and offices were not overfilled; officials maintained their integrity and households their honor; the court had surplus revenue and the people had surplus grain.

sentences.zh: 下忠於上，上禮於下，委裘而無倉卒之危，垂拱而無顛沛之患。

translations.literal: Below were loyal to above, above courteous to below; draping the fur garment without sudden crisis, bowing in repose without overturning calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects were loyal and rulers respectful; the throne could rest at ease without sudden peril, govern with folded hands without fear of upheaval.

sentences.zh: 夫事有惕耳目，動心慮，作不師古，以行於今者，蓋有之矣。

translations.literal: Affairs that alert the eyes and ears and move the heart and thought, acting not taking antiquity as master to carry out in the present—probably have existed.
translations.idiomatic: There have always been policies that startle the eye and trouble the mind—measures that break with ancient precedent and impose themselves on the present age.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下百倍行賞，十倍增官，金銀不供其印，束帛無充於錫，何愧於無用之臣，何慚於無力之士！

translations.literal: I humbly consider Your Majesty conducts rewards a hundredfold, increases offices tenfold; gold and silver cannot supply the seals, silk bundles cannot fill the bestowals—what shame at useless ministers, what modesty at powerless scholars!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty now bestows rewards a hundred times over and multiplies offices tenfold—gold and silver cannot keep pace with the seals, silk cannot keep pace with the grants. What shame is there in useless ministers? What modesty in powerless men of talent!

sentences.zh: 至於公府補授，罕有推擇，遂使富商豪賈，盡居纓冕之流，鬻伎行巫，鹹涉膏腴之地。

translations.literal: As for government office appointments and grants, rarely are there promotions and selections; thus causing wealthy merchants and magnates all to occupy cap-and-girdle ranks, selling skills and practicing shamanism all to involve fertile lands.
translations.idiomatic: As for appointments to government posts, selection is scarcely exercised at all, so that wealthy merchants and magnates fill the ranks of officialdom, while performers and shamans hold lucrative posts on fertile lands.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古人曰：「福生有基，禍生有胎。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard the ancients say: "Fortune born has foundation, calamity born has embryo."
translations.idiomatic: I recall the ancients' saying: "Blessing has its roots, and disaster its beginnings."

sentences.zh: 伏惟公主陛下之愛女，選賢良以嫁之，設官職以輔之，傾府庫以賜之，壯第觀以居之，廣池膋以嬉之，可謂之至重也，可謂之至憐也。

translations.literal: I humbly consider the princess is Your Majesty's beloved daughter—select worthy and good to marry her, establish official posts to assist her, pour the treasury to bestow on her, grand mansion and tower to dwell in, broad pools and fattened meat to amuse her—this can be called utmost weight, utmost pity.
translations.idiomatic: The princess is Your Majesty's beloved daughter: you chose a husband for her, appointed officials to serve her, poured out the treasury in gifts, gave her a splendid mansion to live in and broad ponds for her pleasure. By any measure this is the utmost favor and the utmost tenderness.

sentences.zh: 然而用不合於古義，行不根於人心，將恐變愛成憎，轉福為禍。

translations.literal: However, employment not conforming to ancient meaning, conduct not rooted in popular mind—I fear changing love into hatred, turning fortune into calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these measures accord with neither ancient principle nor the people's hearts. I fear that love may turn to hatred and blessing to disaster.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 竭人之力，人怨也；

translations.literal: Exhausting people's strength—people's resentment;
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust the people's labor is to earn their resentment;

sentences.zh: 費人之財，人怨也；

translations.literal: Expending people's wealth—people's resentment;
translations.idiomatic: to squander the people's wealth is to earn their resentment;

sentences.zh: 奪人之家，人怨也。

translations.literal: Seizing people's homes—people's resentment.
translations.idiomatic: to seize the people's homes is to earn their resentment.

sentences.zh: 愛數子而取三怨於天下，使邊疆之士不盡力，朝廷之士不盡忠，人之散矣，獨持所愛，何所恃乎？

translations.literal: Loving several children yet taking three resentments under heaven, making frontier warriors not exert full strength, court scholars not exert full loyalty—people scattered, alone holding what is loved; what is there to rely on?
translations.idiomatic: To cherish a few favorites while earning threefold resentment throughout the realm is to leave frontier soldiers unwilling to fight their hardest and court officials unwilling to serve their fullest. When the people are alienated, what can Your Majesty rely upon but those few you favor?

sentences.zh: 向者魯王賞同諸婿，禮等朝臣，則亦有今日之福，無曩時之禍。

translations.literal: Formerly the Prince of Lu's rewards were equal to son-in-laws, rituals equal to court ministers—then he also had today's fortune, without former calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu was rewarded no more lavishly than other imperial sons-in-law and treated with the same ceremony as court ministers, he enjoyed the blessings of the present without the disasters of the past.

sentences.zh: 人徒見其禍，不知禍之所來。

translations.literal: People only see the calamity, not knowing where calamity comes from.
translations.idiomatic: People see only the disaster, not the source from which it springs.

sentences.zh: 所以禍者，寵愛過於臣子也。

translations.literal: The reason for calamity is that favor and love exceeded ministers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: The source of disaster is favor lavished beyond what is due even to ministers and sons.

sentences.zh: 去年七月五日，已見其征矣。

translations.literal: Last year, on the fifth day of the seventh month, its sign was already seen.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the seventh month last year, the warning was already plain.

sentences.zh: 而今事無改，更尚因循，棄一宅而造一宅，忘前禍而忽後禍。

translations.literal: Now matters have not changed; instead you still cling to delay—abandoning one residence to build another, forgetting former calamity while neglecting later calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet nothing has changed: you still trifle and delay, abandoning one mansion only to build another, forgetting past disasters while ignoring those still to come.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂陛下憎之矣，非愛之也。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say Your Majesty hates them—not love.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say, Your Majesty, that you bear them hatred, not love.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君以人為本，本固則邦寧。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: the ruler takes people as foundation; when the foundation is firm, then the state is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a ruler takes the people as his foundation; when that foundation is firm, the realm is secure.

sentences.zh: 邦寧則陛下夫婦、母子長相保也。

translations.literal: When the state is at peace, then Your Majesty's husband and wife, mother and son, long preserve one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is secure, Your Majesty's marriage and the bond between mother and son can long endure.

sentences.zh: 伏惟外謀宰臣，為久安之計以存之，不使奸臣賊子以伺之。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider: outwardly consult chief ministers, make a plan for long peace to preserve them, not allow treacherous ministers and wicked sons to watch for openings.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to consult your chief ministers openly and devise a plan for lasting stability, so that treacherous officials and corrupt princes may not lie in wait.

sentences.zh: 臣聞微不可不防，遠不可不慮。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: the subtle must not go undefended; the distant must not go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that what seems slight must still be guarded against, and what seems distant must still be weighed in advance.

sentences.zh: 當今疆場危駭，倉廩空虛，揭竿守禦之士賞不及，肝腦塗地之卒輸不充。

translations.literal: At present the frontiers are dangerously alarmed, granaries empty and void; warriors who raise poles to defend and guard do not receive rewards, soldiers who spill liver and brains on the ground do not have their provisions supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Today the frontiers are in peril and the granaries stand empty; soldiers who take up arms in defense go unrewarded, and men who shed their blood on the battlefield go unsupplied.

sentences.zh: 而方大起寺舍，廣造第宅，伐木空山，不足充梁棟，運土塞路，不足充墻壁。

translations.literal: Yet just now greatly raising monasteries and dwellings, broadly building mansions—felling trees empties mountains, not enough to fill beams and pillars; transporting earth blocks roads, not enough to fill walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are building monasteries on a grand scale and erecting vast mansions—stripping mountains bare of timber that still cannot supply your beams and pillars, hauling earth until roads are choked and still not enough to raise your walls.

sentences.zh: 誇古耀今，逾章越制，百僚鉗口四海傷心。

translations.literal: Boasting of antiquity, dazzling the present, exceeding regulations and overstepping standards—the hundred officials' mouths are clamped shut, and within the four seas hearts are wounded.
translations.idiomatic: You boast of surpassing the ancients and outshining the present, violating statute and exceeding precedent; the hundred officials dare not speak, and hearts ache throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫釋教者，以清凈為基，慈悲為主，故當體道以濟物，不欲利己以損人，故常去己以全真，不為榮身以害教。

translations.literal: Now Buddhism takes purity and stillness as foundation, compassion as master; therefore one ought to embody the Way to aid things, not desire to benefit the self to harm others; therefore one constantly removes the self to preserve wholeness, not act to glorify the body and harm the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism takes purity as its foundation and compassion as its principle; one should embody the Way to aid the world, not profit oneself at others' expense, and set aside the self to preserve the whole, not adorn one's person to the detriment of the faith.

sentences.zh: 三時之月，掘山穿池，損命也；

translations.literal: In the months of the three seasons, digging mountains and piercing pools—harm to life;
translations.idiomatic: To dig into mountains and excavate ponds during the working seasons is to destroy life;

sentences.zh: 殫府虛帑，損人也；

translations.literal: Exhausting the treasury and emptying coffers—harm to people;
translations.idiomatic: to drain the treasury is to harm the people;

sentences.zh: 廣殿長廊，榮身也。

translations.literal: Broad halls and long corridors—glorifying the body.
translations.idiomatic: to raise vast halls and endless corridors is to glorify oneself.

sentences.zh: 損命則不慈悲，損人則不濟物，榮身則不清凈，豈大聖大神之心乎！

translations.literal: Harming life then is not compassion; harming people is not aiding things; glorifying the body is not purity and stillness—is this the mind of the great sage and great spirit!
translations.idiomatic: To destroy life is not compassion; to harm the people is not to aid the world; to glorify oneself is not purity—can this be the mind of the Great Sage?

sentences.zh: 臣以為非真教，非佛意，違時行，違人欲。

translations.literal: Your subject considers this is not the true teaching, not the Buddha's intent; it violates the season's practice and violates people's desires.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this is neither true religion nor the Buddha's will; it runs counter to the times and against the people's wishes.

sentences.zh: 自像王西下，佛教東傳，青螺不入於周前，白馬方行於漢後。

translations.literal: Since the Image-King went west, Buddhism spread east—the blue-snail shell did not enter before Zhou; the white horse only traveled after Han.
translations.idiomatic: Since Śākyamuni went west and Buddhism spread eastward, the faith did not reach China before the Zhou, and the White Horse only arrived after the Han.

sentences.zh: 風流雨散，千帝百王，飾彌盛而國彌空，役彌重而禍彌大。

translations.literal: Scattered like wind and rain, a thousand emperors and hundred kings—ornamentation ever more lavish while the state ever more empty, corvée ever heavier while calamity ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty has seen this pattern: the more lavish the display, the emptier the treasury; the heavier the forced labor, the greater the disaster.

sentences.zh: 覆車繼軌，曾不改途，晉臣以佞佛取譏，梁主以舍身構隙。

translations.literal: Overturned carts follow one after another in the tracks, never altering the path—Jin ministers were mocked for toadying to Buddhism; Liang rulers created rifts by offering their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: One overturned cart after another has taken the same road, and no ruler has changed course—Jin ministers were mocked for flattering Buddhism, Liang emperors brought ruin by offering their bodies to the faith.

sentences.zh: 若以造寺必為其理體，養人不足以經邦，則殷、周已往皆暗亂，漢、魏已降皆聖明；

translations.literal: If building monasteries must be the principle of governing, and nourishing people is insufficient to administer the state, then before Yin and Zhou all was dark disorder, and from Han and Wei onward all was sage and bright;
translations.idiomatic: If building temples were truly the principle of good government, and caring for the people were insufficient to rule the realm, then everything before the Yin and Zhou would have been benighted chaos, and everything from the Han and Wei onward would have been sage rule;

sentences.zh: 殷、周已往為不長，漢、魏已降為不短。

translations.literal: Before Yin and Zhou would have been not long, from Han and Wei onward would have been not short.
translations.idiomatic: the eras before Yin and Zhou would have been brief, and those from Han and Wei onward would have been enduring.

sentences.zh: 臣聞夏為天子二十餘代而殷受之，殷為天子二十餘代而周受之，周為天子三十餘代而秦受之，自漢已後歷代可知也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: Xia as Son of Heaven for twenty-odd generations, then Yin received it; Yin as Son of Heaven for twenty-odd generations, then Zhou received it; Zhou as Son of Heaven for thirty-odd generations, then Qin received it; from Han onward the dynasties can be known.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Xia ruled as Son of Heaven for more than twenty generations before Yin succeeded it; Yin ruled for more than twenty generations before Zhou succeeded it; Zhou ruled for more than thirty generations before Qin succeeded it—and from the Han onward the succession is known in detail.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 有道之長，無道之短，豈因其窮金玉、修塔廟，方得久長之祚乎！

translations.literal: Those with the Way endure long; those without the Way are brief—how could exhausting gold and jade and building pagodas and temples be the way to obtain enduring fortune!
translations.idiomatic: States guided by the Way endure; those without it perish quickly—surely long reigns are not won by squandering gold and jade on pagodas and temples!

sentences.zh: 臣聞於經曰：「菩薩心住於法而行布施，如人入暗，即無所見。」

translations.literal: Your subject has heard in the sutras: 'When a bodhisattva's mind dwells in dharmas while practicing giving, it is like a person entering darkness—he sees nothing.'
translations.idiomatic: I have read in the sutras: 'When a bodhisattva's mind clings to phenomena even as he gives alms, it is like a man entering darkness—he sees nothing.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「一切有為法，如夢幻泡影，如露亦如電。」

translations.literal: It also says: 'All conditioned dharmas are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, like dew and also like lightning.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'All conditioned things are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows, like dew and like lightning.'

sentences.zh: 臣以減雕琢之費以賑貧下，是有如來之德；

translations.literal: Your subject considers that reducing carving and ornamentation expenses to relieve the poor below—this has the virtue of the Tathāgata;
translations.idiomatic: I believe that cutting the cost of ornamentation to relieve the poor is to act with the Tathāgata's virtue;

sentences.zh: 息穿掘之苦以全昆蟲，是有如來之仁；

translations.literal: Ceasing the suffering of digging and piercing to preserve insects—this has the Tathāgata's benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: to stop the torment of excavation and preserve even the smallest creatures is to act with the Tathāgata's benevolence;

sentences.zh: 罷營構之直以給邊陲，是有湯、武之功；

translations.literal: Stopping construction wages to supply the frontiers—this has the achievement of Tang and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: to halt construction spending and supply the frontiers is to achieve what Tang and Wu achieved;

sentences.zh: 回不急之祿以購廉清，是有唐、虞之理。

translations.literal: Returning unurgent salaries to purchase integrity and purity—this has the governance of Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: to redirect unneeded stipends toward rewarding honest officials is to govern as Tang and Yu governed.

sentences.zh: 陛下緩其所急，急其所緩，親未來而疏見在，失真實而冀虛無，重俗人之所為而輕天子之功業，臣竊痛之矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty slackens what is urgent, hurries what is slack, is close to what has not come and distant from what is present, loses what is real and hopes for emptiness and nothingness, values what vulgar people do and lightly esteems the Son of Heaven's achievements—your subject secretly grieves.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty treats the urgent as leisurely and the leisurely as urgent, cherishes what lies ahead while neglecting what is at hand, abandons the real for the empty, and esteems the pursuits of common men above the Son of Heaven's true work—I grieve to see it.

sentences.zh: 當今出財依勢者盡度為沙門，避役奸訛者盡度為沙門；

translations.literal: At present those who pay out wealth and rely on influence are all ordained as monks; those who evade corvée with deceit and fraud are all ordained as monks;
translations.idiomatic: Today everyone who pays bribes and trades on influence is ordained a monk; everyone who evades corvée through fraud is ordained a monk;

sentences.zh: 其所未度，唯貧窮與善人。

translations.literal: Those not yet ordained are only the poor and the good people.
translations.idiomatic: only the poor and the honest remain unordained.

sentences.zh: 將何以作範乎？

translations.literal: With what will you make a model?
translations.idiomatic: What standard will this set?

sentences.zh: 將何以役力乎？

translations.literal: With what will you employ labor power?
translations.idiomatic: From whom will you draw labor?

sentences.zh: 臣以為出家者，舍塵俗，離朋黨，無私愛。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that one who leaves home abandons the dusty world, departs from factions, and has no private loves.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that to leave home is to renounce the world of dust, leave behind factions, and harbor no private attachments.

sentences.zh: 今殖貨營生，非舍塵俗；

translations.literal: Now amassing goods and managing livelihood—this is not abandoning the dusty world;
translations.idiomatic: Yet today they amass wealth and pursue trade—this is not renouncing the world;

sentences.zh: 拔親樹知，非離朋黨；

translations.literal: Pulling up kin and planting favorites—this is not departing from factions;
translations.idiomatic: they favor relatives and cultivate cronies—this is not leaving factions behind;

sentences.zh: 畜妻養孥，非無私愛。

translations.literal: Keeping wives and rearing children—this is not having no private loves.
translations.idiomatic: they keep wives and raise children—this is not freedom from private attachment.

sentences.zh: 是致人以毀道，非廣道以求人。

translations.literal: This is causing people to destroy the Way, not broadening the Way to seek people.
translations.idiomatic: This invites men to ruin the Way rather than spreading the Way to embrace men.

sentences.zh: 伏見今之宮觀臺榭，京師之與洛陽，不增修飾，猶恐奢麗。

translations.literal: I respectfully observe that today's palaces, towers, and pavilions—in the capital and in Luoyang—even without added ornament, still fear extravagance and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the palaces and towers of the capital and Luoyang, even without further embellishment, already verge on excess.

sentences.zh: 陛下尚欲填池塹，捐苑囿，以賑貧人無產業者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty still wishes to fill in pools and ditches, surrender parks and preserves, to relieve poor people without property.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has even spoken of filling in ponds, surrendering parklands, and using the proceeds to aid the destitute.

sentences.zh: 今天下之寺蓋無其數，一寺當陛下一宮，壯麗之甚矣！

translations.literal: Today monasteries under heaven surely are beyond counting; one monastery equals one of Your Majesty's palaces—how exceedingly grand and splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries throughout the realm are beyond number; a single temple rivals one of Your Majesty's palaces in grandeur!

sentences.zh: 用度過之矣！

translations.literal: Expenditure surpasses it!
translations.idiomatic: Their cost surpasses it!

sentences.zh: 是十分天下之財而佛有七八，陛下何有之矣！

translations.literal: This is dividing ten parts of the realm's wealth, and the Buddha possesses seven or eight—what does Your Majesty have left!
translations.idiomatic: If the realm's wealth were divided into ten parts, seven or eight would belong to Buddhism—what remains for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 百姓何食之矣！

translations.literal: What will the common people eat!
translations.idiomatic: What will the common people live on!

sentences.zh: 雖以陰陽為炭，萬物為銅，役不食之人，使不衣之士，猶尚不給。

translations.literal: Even if using yin and yang as charcoal and the ten thousand things as copper, employing men who do not eat, making scholars who do not wear clothes, still it would not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Even if yin and yang were your fuel and the ten thousand things your ore, even if you conscripted men who need no food and workers who need no clothing, it would still not suffice.

sentences.zh: 況資於天生地養，風動雨潤，而後得之乎！

translations.literal: How much more when relying on what heaven generates and earth nourishes, moved by wind and moistened by rain, and only afterward obtaining it!
translations.idiomatic: How much less when wealth must come from what heaven and earth provide, ripened by wind and rain!

sentences.zh: 臣聞國無九年之儲，國非其國。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: when a state lacks nine years' stores, the state is not its state.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a state lacks nine years' reserves, it is no true state at all.

sentences.zh: 伏計倉廩，度府庫，百僚供給，百事用度，臣恐卒歲不充，況九年之積乎！

translations.literal: I respectfully calculate granaries, estimate treasuries, officials' provisions, and the hundred affairs' expenditures—your subject fears it will not suffice for the year's end, how much less nine years' accumulation!
translations.idiomatic: When I reckon the granaries, estimate the treasuries, and tally the stipends of officials and the costs of every affair, I fear we cannot finish the year—let alone accumulate nine years' supply!

sentences.zh: 一旦風塵再擾，霜雹薦臻，沙門不可擐干戈，寺塔不足攘饑饉，臣竊痛之矣！

translations.literal: Once wind and dust are disturbed again, frost and hail come repeatedly, monks cannot don armor, temples and pagodas cannot repel famine—your subject secretly grieves!
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil returns and frost and hail strike again, monks cannot take up arms, and temples cannot stave off famine—I grieve to think of it!

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and rejected.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，安樂公主被誅。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Princess Anle was executed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Princess Anle was put to death.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，又為金仙、玉真公主廣營二觀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, construction was again expanded on the two monasteries for the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected princesses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, construction again expanded on the two monasteries for the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected princesses.

sentences.zh: 先是，中宗時斜封受官人一切停任，凡數百千人，又有敕放令卻上。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the time of Emperor Zhongzong, all those who had received office through irregular sealed appointments had been dismissed—several hundred or a thousand in all—and there was also an edict releasing them to return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Emperor Zhongzong, all who had received office through irregular sealed appointments had been dismissed—several hundred or more—and an edict then allowed them to return.

sentences.zh: 替否時為左補闕，又上疏陳時政曰：

translations.literal: Tifou was then Left Remonstrator and again submitted a memorial setting forth current policy, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou was then Left Remonstrator and again memorialized on current policy, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣嘗以為古之用度不時，爵賞不當，破家亡國者，口說不如身逢，耳聞不如眼見，臣請以有唐已來理國之得失，陛下之所眼見者以言之。

translations.literal: Your subject once considered that in antiquity, those who through untimely expenditures and improper rewards and titles brought ruin to family and state—hearing is not equal to encountering it oneself, seeing with the eyes is not equal to hearing with the ears; your subject requests to take the gains and losses of governing since Tang began, what Your Majesty has seen with his own eyes, and speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: I have long believed that in antiquity, rulers who spent at the wrong time and rewarded office without merit brought ruin upon their houses and realms—yet to hear of disaster is not like living through it, and to hear tell is not like seeing with one's own eyes. I ask leave to speak of the successes and failures of Tang governance that Your Majesty has witnessed firsthand.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下審之聽之，擇善而從之，則萬歲之業，自可致矣，何憂乎黎庶之不康，福祚之不永！

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty carefully examines and listens, choosing what is good and following it, then the enterprise of ten thousand years can naturally be attained—why worry that the common people will not be at peace, or that fortune and tenure will not be enduring!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will examine these matters carefully, listen closely, and follow what is good, the work of an enduring reign may be achieved—why fear that the people will not prosper or that fortune will not last!

sentences.zh: 伏以太宗文武聖皇帝，陛下之祖，撥亂反正，開階立極，得至理之體，設簡要之方。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Emperor Taizong the Civil and Military Sage Emperor, Your Majesty's ancestor, quelled disorder and restored correctness, opened the steps and established the foundation, obtained the substance of supreme governance, and set forth simple and essential methods.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully recall Emperor Taizong, the Civil and Military Sage, Your Majesty's ancestor, who quelled chaos, restored order, founded the dynasty, grasped the essence of true governance, and established simple, effective methods.

sentences.zh: 省其官，清其吏，舉天下職司無一虛授，用天下財帛無一枉費。

translations.literal: He reduced offices, purified officials; throughout the realm not one post was filled in vain, not one coin of the realm's wealth was spent wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: He trimmed the bureaucracy and purged corrupt officials; throughout the realm no office was filled without cause and no coin of public wealth was wasted.

sentences.zh: 賞必俟功，官必得俊，所為無不成，所征無不伏。

translations.literal: Rewards awaited merit; offices obtained the talented; what was undertaken none failed, what was dispatched none did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards followed merit; offices went to the worthy; nothing he undertook failed, and no foe he sent armies against failed to submit.

sentences.zh: 不多造寺觀而福德自至，不多度僧尼而殃咎自滅。

translations.literal: He did not build many temples and monasteries, yet merit and fortune came of themselves; he did not ordain many monks and nuns, yet misfortune and blame vanished of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He did not erect countless temples, yet blessings came unbidden; he did not ordain vast numbers of monks and nuns, yet calamity faded away.

sentences.zh: 道合乎天地，德通乎神明。

translations.literal: His Way accorded with Heaven and Earth; his virtue penetrated to the divine spirits.
translations.idiomatic: His Way accorded with Heaven and Earth; his virtue reached the spirits.

sentences.zh: 故天地憐之，神明祐之，使陰陽不愆，風雨合度。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth pitied him, the divine spirits protected him, making yin and yang without error, wind and rain in proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth favored him and the spirits protected him; yin and yang kept their balance, and wind and rain came in season.

sentences.zh: 四人樂其業，五谷遂其成，腐粟爛帛，填街委巷。

translations.literal: The four classes rejoiced in their occupations, the five grains achieved their ripening; rotted grain and worn silk filled streets and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: The four classes of people prospered in their trades, the five grains ripened in abundance, and spoiled grain and worn cloth littered the streets.

sentences.zh: 千里萬里，貢賦於郊；

translations.literal: For a thousand li and ten thousand li, tribute and taxes arrived at the suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: From every corner of the realm tribute and taxes flowed to the capital;

sentences.zh: 九夷百蠻，歸款於闕。

translations.literal: The nine barbarians and hundred man tribes submitted allegiance at the court.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians near and far came to pay homage at the throne.

sentences.zh: 自有帝皇已來，未有若斯之神聖者也，故得享國久長，多歷年所，陛下何不取而則之？

translations.literal: Since emperors and kings have existed, none has been so divine and sage; therefore he enjoyed the state long and endured, passing through many years—why does Your Majesty not take him and use him as model?
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of emperors, none has been so truly sage; his reign was long and enduring. Why does Your Majesty not take him as your model?

sentences.zh: 中宗孝和皇帝，陛下之兄，居先人之業，忽先人之化，不取賢良之言，而恣子女之意。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong the Filial and Harmonious Emperor, Your Majesty's elder brother, occupied the former men's enterprise, suddenly the former men's transformation, did not take worthy words but indulged the will of sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong, the Filial and Harmonious, Your Majesty's elder brother, inherited their forefathers' legacy yet forgot their example; he heeded no counsel of the worthy but indulged his children as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 官爵非擇，虛食祿者數千人；

translations.literal: Offices and ranks were not chosen; those eating salary in vain numbered in the thousands;
translations.idiomatic: He handed out offices and titles without discrimination; thousands ate stipends for no work;

sentences.zh: 封建無功，妄食土者百餘戶。

translations.literal: Enfeoffments without merit—more than a hundred households ate land in vain.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed the undeserving; more than a hundred households received fiefs without merit.

sentences.zh: 造寺不止，枉費財者數百億；

translations.literal: Building monasteries without end—wrongly spent wealth numbered in the hundreds of millions;
translations.idiomatic: He never stopped building temples, squandering hundreds of millions in public funds;

sentences.zh: 度人不休，免租庸者數十萬。

translations.literal: Ordaining people without rest—those exempted from tax and corvée numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: he never ceased ordaining clergy, exempting tens of thousands from tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 是使國家所出加數倍，所入減數倍。

translations.literal: This made what the state disbursed increase severalfold, what it received decrease severalfold.
translations.idiomatic: State expenditures multiplied while revenues shrank.

sentences.zh: 倉不停卒歲之儲，庫不貯一時之帛。

translations.literal: Granaries did not hold stores for the year's end; treasuries did not store silks for a season.
translations.idiomatic: The granaries held no surplus for the year; the treasuries no reserve even for a season.

sentences.zh: 所惡者逐，逐多忠良；

translations.literal: Those he hated he drove away—those driven away were mostly loyal and good;
translations.idiomatic: Those he hated were driven out—and those driven out were mostly the loyal and good;

sentences.zh: 所愛者賞，賞多讒慝。

translations.literal: Those he loved he rewarded—those rewarded were mostly many slanderers and villains.
translations.idiomatic: those he favored were rewarded—and those rewarded were mostly slanderers and villains.

sentences.zh: 朋佞喋喋，交相傾動。

translations.literal: Factions of flatterers chattered incessantly, mutually overthrowing and agitating.
translations.idiomatic: Factions of flatterers chattered endlessly, undermining one another.

sentences.zh: 容身不為於朝廷，保位皆由於黨附。

translations.literal: Preserving the body was not done in the court; preserving position all came from faction attachment.
translations.idiomatic: They sought not to serve the court but to keep their posts through faction and patronage.

sentences.zh: 奪百姓之食，以養殘兇；

translations.literal: Seizing the common people's food to nourish the crippled and vicious;
translations.idiomatic: They seized the people's food to nourish the wicked;

sentences.zh: 剝萬人之衣，以塗土木。

translations.literal: Stripping ten thousand people's garments to smear earth and wood.
translations.idiomatic: they stripped the people's clothing to gild their temples in earth and wood.

sentences.zh: 於是人怨神怒，親忿眾離，水旱不調，疾疫屢起。

translations.literal: Then people's resentment and the divine spirits' anger, kin's resentment and the masses' scattering—water and drought not in harmony, pestilence repeatedly arising.
translations.idiomatic: Man's resentment and the spirits' wrath followed; kin turned against him and the people deserted him; floods and droughts came, and plague returned again and again.

sentences.zh: 遠近殊論，公私罄然。

translations.literal: Near and far had different discourses; public and private were utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion divided near and far; public and private resources were alike exhausted.

sentences.zh: 五六年間，再三禍變，享國不永，受終於兇婦人。

translations.literal: Within five or six years, calamity and change came again and again; enjoying the state was not enduring—he received his end at the hands of a vicious woman.
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years disaster struck again and again; his reign was brief, and he met his end at the hands of a wicked woman.

sentences.zh: 寺舍不能保其身，僧尼不能護妻子，取譏萬代，見笑四夷。

translations.literal: Monasteries could not preserve his person; monks and nuns could not protect wives and children—drawing mockery for ten thousand generations, seen laughing by the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Temples could not save him; monks could not protect his wife and children; he became a mockery for ages and a laughingstock among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 此陛下之所眼見也，何不除而改之。

translations.literal: This is what Your Majesty has seen with his eyes—why not remove it and change it?
translations.idiomatic: This Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes—why not cast it off and change course?

sentences.zh: 依太宗之理國，則百官以理，百姓無憂，故太山之安立可致矣；

translations.literal: Following Taizong's governing of the state, then the hundred officials are governed by principle, the common people without worry—therefore Mount Tai's security can immediately be attained;
translations.idiomatic: Follow Taizong's way of governing, and the hundred officials will be ruled by principle, the people will know no fear—Mount Tai's security can be achieved at once;

sentences.zh: 依中宗之理國，則萬人以怨，百事不寧，故累卵之危立可致矣。

translations.literal: Following Zhongzong's governing of the state, then ten thousand people resent, the hundred affairs not at peace—therefore the danger of piled eggs can immediately be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Zhongzong's way, and ten thousand people will resent, the hundred affairs will know no peace—and the danger of a tower of eggs can be achieved at once.

sentences.zh: 頃自夏已來，霪雨不解，谷荒於壟，麥爛於場。

translations.literal: Recently from summer onward, excessive rain has not cleared; grain lies waste in the furrows, wheat rots in the threshing floor.
translations.idiomatic: Since summer, unending rains have ruined the grain in the fields and rotted the wheat on the threshing floors.

sentences.zh: 入秋已來，亢旱成災，苗而不實，霜損蟲暴，草葉枯黃。

translations.literal: From autumn onward, severe drought became disaster; seedlings bore no fruit, frost damaged and insects ravaged, grass and leaves withered yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn, severe drought has struck; crops failed to ripen, frost and pests destroyed what remained, and grass and leaves withered brown.

sentences.zh: 下人咨嗟，未知赒賑；

translations.literal: The lower people sigh and lament, not knowing relief and relief distribution;
translations.idiomatic: The people groan in distress, uncertain whether relief will come;

sentences.zh: 而營寺造觀，日繼於時，檢校試官，充臺溢署。

translations.literal: Yet building monasteries and constructing monasteries daily continues in season; inspecting and testing officials fill posts beyond count at the terraces and overflow offices.
translations.idiomatic: yet monasteries and temples rise day after day, and provisional inspectors and examiners overflow the offices of the terraces.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下愛兩女，為造兩觀，燒瓦運木，載土填坑，道路流言，皆云計用錢百餘萬貫。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty loves two daughters, and for them builds two monasteries; burning tiles and transporting wood, loading earth and filling pits—roadside rumors all say the planned expenditure exceeds a million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: I know Your Majesty loves your two daughters and is building two monasteries for them—firing tiles, hauling timber, loading earth and filling pits; rumor in the streets puts the cost at more than a million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下，聖人也，無所不知；

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty is the sage person, nothing not known;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage and knows all things;

sentences.zh: 陛下，明君也，無所不見。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the enlightened ruler, nothing not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is enlightened and sees all things.

sentences.zh: 既知且見，知倉有幾年之儲，庫有幾年之帛？

translations.literal: Since you know and see, do you know how many years' stores the granaries hold, how many years' silks the treasuries hold?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing this, do you know how many years' grain the granaries hold, how many years' silk the treasuries hold?

sentences.zh: 知百姓之間可存活乎？

translations.literal: Do you know whether among the common people survival is possible?
translations.idiomatic: Do you know whether the people can survive?

sentences.zh: 三邊之上可轉輸乎？

translations.literal: On the three frontiers can transport be transferred?
translations.idiomatic: Can supplies reach the three frontiers?

sentences.zh: 當今發一卒以禦邊陲，遣一兵以衛社稷，多無衣食，皆帶饑寒。

translations.literal: At present, dispatching one soldier to defend the frontiers, sending one trooper to guard the altars of state—many lack food and clothing, all bear hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Today, to send one soldier to the frontier or one guardsman to defend the realm, most go without food or clothing and all endure hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 賞賜之間，迥無所出，軍旅驟敗，莫不由斯。

translations.literal: Among rewards and grants, utterly nothing to disburse; armies suddenly defeated—none not from this.
translations.idiomatic: There is nothing left for rewards; armies fail in battle—and none of it is unconnected to this.

sentences.zh: 而乃以百萬貫錢造無用之觀，以受六合之怨乎！

translations.literal: Yet you use a million strings of cash to build useless monasteries—to receive resentment from the six directions!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would spend a million strings of cash on useless monasteries and earn the resentment of all under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 以違萬人之心乎！

translations.literal: To go against the hearts of ten thousand people!
translations.idiomatic: To defy the will of ten thousand people!

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下續阿韋之醜跡，而不改阿韋之亂政。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty continues Empress Wei and Consort Wei's ugly tracks, yet does not change Empress Wei and Consort Wei's disorderly government.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that Your Majesty follows in Empress Wei's disgraceful path yet has not abandoned Empress Wei's corrupt rule.

sentences.zh: 忍棄太宗之理本，不忍棄中宗之亂階；

translations.literal: You can bear to abandon Taizong's governing principle and foundation, yet cannot bear to abandon Zhongzong's disorderly steps;
translations.idiomatic: You can abandon Taizong's foundation of good governance, yet cannot abandon Zhongzong's ruinous ways;

sentences.zh: 忍棄太宗久長之謀，不忍棄中宗短促之計。

translations.literal: You can bear to abandon Taizong's long-term plans, yet cannot bear to abandon Zhongzong's short-sighted schemes.
translations.idiomatic: You can abandon Taizong's far-sighted designs, yet cannot abandon Zhongzong's shortsighted schemes.

sentences.zh: 陛下又何以繼祖宗、觀萬國。

translations.literal: Your Majesty again with what inherit from ancestors and oversee the myriad states?
translations.idiomatic: How then, Your Majesty, can you carry on your ancestors' legacy and look upon all the realm?

sentences.zh: 昔陛下為皇太子，在阿韋之時，危亡是懼，常切齒於群兇。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Your Majesty was crown prince, in the time of Empress Wei and Consort Wei, peril and ruin were feared; you constantly gnashed your teeth at the evil-doers.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was crown prince, in the days of Empress Wei and Consort Wei, you lived in fear of ruin and often gnashed your teeth at the villains.

sentences.zh: 今貴為天子，富有海內，而不改群兇之事，臣恐復有切齒於陛下者也，陛下又何以非群兇而誅之？

translations.literal: Now exalted as Son of Heaven, rich with all within the seas, yet you do not change the evil-doers' affairs—I fear there will again be those who gnash their teeth at Your Majesty. With what, Your Majesty, can you condemn the evil-doers and execute them?
translations.idiomatic: Now you are exalted as emperor and possess the whole realm, yet you have not changed the ways of those villains. I fear others will gnash their teeth at you again. How then can Your Majesty denounce such villains and punish them?

sentences.zh: 臣往見明敕，自今已後，一依貞觀故事。

translations.literal: Your subject formerly saw a clear edict: from now onward, entirely follow Zhenguan precedents.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen Your Majesty's clear edict that from this day forward all should follow the precedents of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 且貞觀之時，豈有今日之造寺營觀，加僧尼道士，益無用之官，行不急之務，而亂政者也！

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Zhenguan era, was there today's building temples and erecting monasteries, adding monks, nuns, and Daoist priests, increasing useless offices, undertaking unurgent tasks, and thereby disordering government!
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, was there ever anything like today's temple-building and monastery construction, the swelling of monks, nuns, and Daoist priests, the multiplication of useless offices, and the pursuit of nonessential tasks that throw government into disorder?

sentences.zh: 臣以為棄其言而不行其信，慕其善而不遷其惡，陛下又何以刑於四海？

translations.literal: Your subject considers that abandoning its words yet not carrying out its faith, admiring its goodness yet not moving away from its evil—with what, Your Majesty, can you be a model to the four seas?
translations.idiomatic: I believe that to discard those words without keeping that pledge, to admire what was good yet not turn from what was evil—how can Your Majesty then set an example for all under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 往者，和帝之憐悖逆也，為奸人之所誤，宗晉卿勸為第宅，趙履溫勸為園亭，損數百家之居，侵數百家之地。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Emperor He had pity on the rebellious prince, he was misled by villains: Zong Jinqing urged the building of mansions, Zhao Lüwen urged the building of gardens and pavilions, damaging the dwellings of several hundred households and encroaching on the lands of several hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Emperor Zhongzong showed pity to the rebellious prince, he was led astray by schemers. Zong Jinqing urged the construction of mansions, and Zhao Lüwen urged the building of gardens and pavilions, ruining the homes of hundreds of families and seizing the lands of hundreds more.

sentences.zh: 工徒斫而未息，義兵紛以交馳，卒使亭不得遊，宅不得坐。

translations.literal: Laborers chopped and did not cease; righteous troops rushed about in confusion; in the end the pavilion could not be visited and the mansion could not be occupied.
translations.idiomatic: Workers still hacked and hewed without pause, loyal troops clashed in turmoil, and in the end the prince could neither stroll in his pavilion nor dwell in his mansion.

sentences.zh: 信邪佞之說，成骨肉之刑，此陛下之所眼見也。

translations.literal: Believing the words of evil flatterers, bringing about punishment among flesh and blood—this Your Majesty saw with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: To heed the counsel of wicked flatterers and bring bloodshed among kin—Your Majesty saw this with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 今茲造觀，臣必知非陛下、公主之本意，得無趙履溫之徒將勸為之，冀誤其骨肉，不可不明察也。

translations.literal: This present building of monasteries—your subject surely knows it is not Your Majesty's and the princess's original intent. Could it not be that men like Zhao Lüwen will urge it, hoping to mislead their flesh and blood? This cannot but be clearly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: This monastery-building, I am certain, is not Your Majesty's or the princess's true intent. Surely men like Zhao Lüwen will urge it on, hoping to lead kin astray. This must be examined with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 臣聞出家修道者，不預人事，專清其身心，以虛泊為高，以無為為妙，依兩卷《老子》，視一軀天尊，無欲無營，不損不害。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that those who leave home to cultivate the Way do not involve themselves in human affairs, but solely purify body and mind, taking emptiness and stillness as lofty, taking nonaction as subtle, relying on the two scrolls of the Laozi, revering a single bodily image of the Heavenly Lord—without desire, without striving, neither harming nor injuring.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who leave the world to cultivate the Way take no part in worldly affairs, but devote themselves to purifying body and mind, holding emptiness and stillness as the highest good and nonaction as the deepest wisdom. They rely on the two scrolls of the Laozi, revere a single image of the Heavenly Lord, and seek neither gain nor ambition, doing no harm to anyone.

sentences.zh: 何必璇臺玉榭，寶像珍龕，使人困窮，然後為道哉！

translations.literal: Why must there be jade towers and jade pavilions, precious images and jeweled shrines, making people destitute—only then is it the Way!
translations.idiomatic: Why must there be jade towers and jade pavilions, precious images and jeweled shrines, driving the people to ruin, before one can call it the Way!

sentences.zh: 且舊觀足可歸依，無造無營，以取窮竭。

translations.literal: Moreover, existing monasteries are sufficient for devotion; do not build, do not undertake construction, thereby bringing exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: The existing monasteries are more than enough for devotion. Build nothing and undertake no new works, lest the realm be driven to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 若此行之三年，國不富，人不安，朝廷不清，陛下不樂，則臣請殺身於朝，以令天下言事者。

translations.literal: If this course is followed for three years and the state is not enriched, the people are not at peace, the court is not clear, and Your Majesty is not pleased, then your subject asks to give his life at court, to instruct all who speak out under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If this policy continues for three years and the state is not enriched, the people are not secure, the court is not set right, and Your Majesty is not content, then I ask to lay down my life at court as a lesson to all who would speak truth to power.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下行非常之惠，權停兩觀，以俟豐年。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty should bestow an extraordinary grace and temporarily halt the two monasteries, awaiting a year of abundance.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully urge Your Majesty to grant an extraordinary act of grace and temporarily halt construction of the two monasteries until a year of plenty.

sentences.zh: 以兩觀之財，為公主施貧窮，填府庫，則公主福德無窮矣。

translations.literal: Using the wealth of the two monasteries to have the princess bestow charity on the poor and fill the treasuries—then the princess's merit and fortune would be boundless.
translations.idiomatic: If the funds for the two monasteries were used to have the princess relieve the poor and replenish the treasury, her merit and blessing would know no end.

sentences.zh: 不然，臣恐下人怨望，不減於前朝之時。

translations.literal: If not so, your subject fears the resentment of those below will be no less than in the former dynasty's time.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I fear the people's resentment will be no less than in the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 前朝之時，賢愚知敗，人雖有口而不敢言，言未發聲，禍將及矣。

translations.literal: In the former dynasty's time, wise and foolish alike knew defeat was coming; people though they had mouths did not dare speak; before words were uttered, disaster was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign, wise and simple alike saw ruin coming. Though people had mouths, they dared not speak; before a word was voiced, calamity was already at hand.

sentences.zh: 韋月將受誅於丹僥，燕欽融見殺於紫庭，此人皆不惜其身而納忠於主，身既死矣，朝亦危矣。

translations.literal: Wei Yuejiang received execution at Danjiao; Yan Qinrong was killed in the Purple Court. These men all did not spare themselves but offered loyalty to their lord. Once their bodies were dead, the court was also in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuejiang was executed at Danjiao, and Yan Qinrong was put to death in the Purple Court. These men did not spare themselves but offered loyal counsel to their sovereign. Once they were dead, the court itself stood in peril.

sentences.zh: 故先朝誅之，陛下賞之，是陛下知直言之士有裨於國。

translations.literal: Therefore the former dynasty executed them, and Your Majesty rewarded them—this shows Your Majesty knows that men of straight speech benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: The previous reign put them to death, yet Your Majesty has honored them—proof that Your Majesty knows men who speak plainly serve the state.

sentences.zh: 臣今直言，亦先代之直，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: Your subject now speaks plainly—it is also the plainness of former generations. Only may Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: What I speak plainly today is the same plain truth offered in former times. I ask only that Your Majesty weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，睿宗嘉其公直。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; Emperor Ruizong praised his public uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong commended his forthright integrity.

sentences.zh: 稍遷為右臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Palace Attendant Investigating Censor of the Right Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Palace Attendant Investigating Censor of the Right Censorate.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累轉潁王府長史。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, he was repeatedly transferred and became Chief Administrator of the Princedom of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he rose through several posts to become Chief Administrator of the Princedom of Ying.

sentences.zh: 天寶初卒，年八十余。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Tianbao era, aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Tianbao reign, at more than eighty years of age.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫好聞其善，惡聞其過，君人者之常情也；

translations.literal: The historian says: To love hearing of one's goodness and hate hearing of one's faults—this is the common disposition of one who rules men;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: To delight in hearing one's virtues praised and to loathe hearing one's faults named is the common disposition of rulers;

sentences.zh: 寧諂媚以取容，不逆耳以招禍，臣人者之常情也。

translations.literal: To prefer flattery to win favor rather than unwelcome words that invite disaster—this is the common disposition of those who serve men.
translations.idiomatic: to prefer flattery that wins favor over blunt counsel that invites disaster is the common disposition of subjects.

sentences.zh: 能反此者，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: To be able to reverse this—is it not also good!
translations.idiomatic: To be able to reverse these tendencies—what could be better!

sentences.zh: 李、薛等六君，吐忠讜之言，補朝廷之失，有犯無隱，不愧古人，有唐之良臣也。

translations.literal: The six gentlemen Li, Xue, and the rest spoke loyal and forthright words, mended the court's failings, offended yet hid nothing, were not ashamed before the ancients—they were good ministers of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xue, and the other five ministers spoke loyal and candid words, remedied the court's failings, and held back nothing even when giving offense. Unashamed before the ancients, they were worthy ministers of Tang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：臣之事君，有邪有正。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: In a subject's service to his lord, there is the crooked and there is the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: In serving one's sovereign, a subject may be crooked or upright.

sentences.zh: 君之使臣，從諫則聖。

translations.literal: In a lord's employment of subjects, to follow remonstrance is to be sage.
translations.idiomatic: In employing his subjects, a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes sage.

sentences.zh: 李、薛輸忠，救人之命。

translations.literal: Li and Xue offered loyalty, saving people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Xue offered loyal counsel and saved lives.

sentences.zh: 韋、韓讜言，醫國之病。

translations.literal: Wei and Han spoke blunt truths, healing the state's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Han spoke blunt truths and healed the nation's ills.

sentences.zh: 辛、王章疏，犯顏竦聽。

translations.literal: Xin and Wang's memorials offended the countenance and made one straighten the ears to listen.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials of Xin and Wang spoke to the ruler's face and made him sit up and listen.

sentences.zh: 張子法言，實裨時政。

translations.literal: Master Zhang's model words truly benefited the governance of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zhang's upright words truly strengthened the governance of the age.
